## 189. A history read off its finite stretches (A4-L)

```text
Result(s): a-history-read-off-its-finite-stretches (new); depends on what-a-finite-history-refutes; related
           becoming-finite-horizon
Delta: section 145 (Becoming.Horizon) stated what a finite history refutes for the runs of every process and left
       IdealWarrant's order form, and the converse of refutable_passes, unstated. IdealWarrant, CompletionRole and
       HistoryIdeals of the completion package proved the order form, the completion and the ideals of histories with
       Std and classical reasoning, outside the run. Here they are one family in the core: a history is the ideal of
       its finite stretches; Horizon's laws are the case of runs of the laws of points; a closed class is the class
       within a lower set, its content; refutable and closed classes pass into each other up to a step that, asked of
       every process, is exactly double-negation elimination; adhering is the least closed class; the completion is
       read at runs; the classification of histories holds for every process, and telling which is LPO
Supplied premises / correspondence: none, no axiom; the classification takes the decision of settling and the picked
       stretches as data; the calibrations take double-negation elimination or LPO as one direction's hypothesis
Evidence: Becoming.Ideals (99 theorems) and Becoming.HistoryIdeals (80), every axiom report empty; core
          receipt `20261019T020248.454200Z`; IdealsCorrespondence, 92 theorems, checked by check_ideals_correspondence.py (receipt
          `20261019T020352.033083Z`), 40 of its 103 declarations with empty reports; connectivity check passes, 466 apart of
          9,895, 25 of them in the two modules, their 18 roots registered
Boundary: what a finite stretch verifies (the open classes) on this order; Boolean tests from the propositional tests a
          closed reading is made of; which readings of an actual unfolding are refutable
```

Ren, 19 October 2026: "integrate all, the theory is a whole, not stitched pieces, go ahead" ([source](../../../../sources/15-codex-theory-conversations/2026-10-19-integrate-all.md)). Decision D45 (4) joined `IdealWarrant` with `CompletionRole` and `HistoryIdeals` as one core family under structural names ([choices](DELEGATED-CHOICES.md#d45-一个说明中的读法--the-readings-in-one-account)), board item A4-L. Ren's "(a)" of 16 October had kept `IdealWarrant` outside the spine (section 153). His words are provenance, not warrant.

**The question.** What a finite history refutes was stated twice: on the runs of every process (`Becoming.Horizon`, section 145) and, classically, on the ideals of any poset (`IdealWarrant`), with the completion (`CompletionRole`) and the ideals of words (`HistoryIdeals`) beside it, outside the run. Are they one law of the unfolding, and what does each classical step say about it?

**The move.** A history is read off its finite stretches. For a process, a stretch is a run with a horizon. One stretch extends another where its horizon is later and the two runs agree up to the earlier one (`stretchOrder`). An ideal of this order is a history: nonempty, closed downward, any two of its stretches extended by a third. A finite history is a principal ideal, and a run is the ideal of the stretches it passes through (`Run.stretches`). `Becoming.Ideals` states the laws for any order. It uses no antisymmetry, so "the same history" is two-way inclusion, not equality. `Becoming.HistoryIdeals` reads them on runs and on words.

**What is proved** (`Becoming.Ideals`, 99 theorems; `Becoming.HistoryIdeals`, 80; no premise).
- *Points and runs.* A reading of points is refutable where every point outside it shows a stretch that no point of the reading passes through. A point adheres to it where each of its stretches is a stretch of a point of the reading. A refutable reading holds, up to double negation, at every adhering point (`Ideals.RefutableBy.not_not`). For runs, refutability and adhering are these at the runs' ideals (`refutable_iff_refutableBy`, `adheres_iff_adheresBy`). So Horizon's `Refutable.not_not`, `Refutable.adheres_least`, `Refutable.adheres_iff`, `not_refutable_of_adheres` and `refutable_adheres_iff` follow from the laws of points (`Stretches.not_not` and the four after it).
- *Closed classes.* A class of ideals is closed (closed downward and under directed unions) exactly where it is the class of the ideals within a lower set of stretches (`Ideals.closed_iff_lower`). That set is unique (`Ideals.lower_unique`) and is the class's content (`Ideals.lower_iff_content`). Read on runs, a reading that holds every run adhering to it is the reading of the runs whose stretches lie in the content of its runs (`closed_iff_within_lower`). It is made of tests, one for each stretch, read as propositions. This is the converse section 145 left: `refutable_passes` reads Boolean tests fixed by prefixes, the converse gives propositional ones, and Boolean ones would need each test decided.
- *Adhering is the least closed class.* A run adheres to a reading exactly where every closed class of histories holding the reading's runs holds it (`Stretches.adheres_iff_closed`). With closure in place of refutability, no double negation is left. The closure is unique (`Stretches.adherence_unique`) and adds no stretch (`Stretches.adheres_content`). It extends any two stretches of an adhering run by one stretch of one run of the reading (`Stretches.adheres_joint`).
- *Refutable and closed.* A refutable class is closed up to double negation (`Ideals.Refutable.closed`). A closed class is refutable where a history known not to lie within it shows a stretch outside (`Ideals.Closed.refutable_iff`). Asked of every order and class, each step is exactly double-negation elimination (`Ideals.refutable_closed_iff`, `Ideals.closed_refutable_iff`). Asked of every process it is too, with witnesses on the process of `()`s (`Stretches.refutable_closed_iff`, `Stretches.closed_refutable_iff`). And a refutable reading holds at every run adhering to it exactly under double-negation elimination (`refutable_holds_iff`, witnessed on the process of Boolean sequences).
- *Avoidance.* The histories avoiding a set of stretches form a closed class (`Ideals.avoids_closed`), the only closed class holding exactly the finite histories that avoid the set (`Ideals.avoids_unique`). It is refutable where every history failing to avoid the set holds a stretch of it (`Ideals.avoids_refutable_of_found`). On runs these are `Stretches.avoids_adheres`, `Stretches.avoids_runs` and `Stretches.avoids_refutable`. These are the safety classes.
- *A lower set's own histories.* The order a lower set inherits has, as its histories, the process's histories within the set (`Ideals.lift_restrict`, `Ideals.restrict_lift`, `Stretches.inherited_histories`). They are ordered as the runs are (`Stretches.within_order_iff`).
- *The completion.* The ideals are directed-complete (`Ideals.idealComplete`) and compact exactly at the finite histories (`Ideals.compact_iff_principal`), so no run is compact (`Stretches.run_not_compact`). A monotone reading of stretches extends to a continuous reading of histories, unique up to the target's equivalence (`Ideals.unique_continuous_extension`). So a continuous reading is fixed at every run by its values on finite histories (`Stretches.run_reading_unique`). The readings "lies above this stretch" tell histories, and runs, apart (`Ideals.above_readings_separate`, `Stretches.runs_told_apart`). The finite histories are a compact basis (`Stretches.finite_basis`). Any directed-complete order with a compact basis copying the stretches is the order of the histories, by an equivalence the stretches fix (`Ideals.unique_basis_representation`, `Stretches.histories_representation`).
- *Which histories are runs.* A history that settles, having a latest stretch, is finite (`Stretches.settles_principal`). One that goes on, with a stretch beyond each horizon picked, is the history of the run read off the picks (`Stretches.pickedRun`, `Stretches.goesOn_run`). So a history that settles, or goes on with picks, is a finite history or a run (`Stretches.classification`: the completion package's A4, for every process). Telling which, on the histories of `()`s cut at a Boolean sequence's first `true`, is exactly the limited principle of omniscience (`Stretches.cut_decided_iff_lpo`, through the word version `HistoryIdeals.cut_decided_iff_lpo`).
- *Words.* Words are ordered by prefix, and a sequence is the ideal of its initial words (`HistoryIdeals.traceIdeal`). A history's ideal lies below another's exactly where it is a prefix of it (`HistoryIdeals.history_le_iff`), and the same words make the same history (`HistoryIdeals.historyIdeal_same_iff`). For the process of all sequences, the runs' histories are these (`Stretches.sequences_le_iff`, `Stretches.sequences_same_iff`, `Stretches.sequences_within_iff`). A prefix-closed language is a lower set of words, so its histories form a closed class (`HistoryIdeals.history_within_iff`). The finite histories with the infinite ones of a property are not refutable where some sequence lies outside the property (`HistoryIdeals.finiteOr_not_refutable`).

**The instance.** `IdealsCorrespondence` (periphery, Lean 4.30.0-rc2, its own checker) reads the three originals as instances. A poset's order is an order of stretches, its antisymmetry unused, and its ideals and classes are the core's. W1, W2, W2a, A2, A2a, A3 and A4 then follow from the core's laws. 40 of its 103 declarations have empty reports. The rest name the classical or extensionality step each needs: the stability, the element outside, the decision of settling and the picks; equalities of predicates, ideals and words. The originals keep their paths and bytes.

**What this changes.** The order form section 145 left unstated is stated, and Horizon's laws are its case of runs: the theory has one law of what a finite stretch refutes, not two. The classical equivalence of finite refutability and Scott closure (W1) is located: it is two steps, and each, asked of every process, is double-negation elimination. Ren's "(a)" of 16 October is superseded by D45 (4), and the directive register notes it.

*Readings* [AI reading]. Not being refuted by any finite stretch is not belonging: a history that no stretch shows outside a class may still not lie in it, and saying it does is the step double negation would take. A history known not to lie within a closed class does not thereby show the stretch at which it leaves. Telling whether a history ends is deciding whether it changes again. What a finite stretch can show is that a history lies outside a closed class; that a run lies in one is only not refuted.

**Not done.** What a finite stretch verifies, the open classes, read on the same order; Boolean tests from the propositional tests a closed reading is made of, which needs each test decided; a world's courses read as histories of this order (through `worlds-are-runs` they are runs).

**Self-review.** The statements were read against the Lean.
- The first build stood apart from the base: 115 of its 139 theorems (`Becoming.Ideals` 94 of 98, `Becoming.HistoryIdeals` 21 of 41), with 50 roots unregistered. Against "the theory is a whole, not stitched pieces", each law of ideals is now read on the histories of a process (`Stretches`). 25 of 179 stand apart: equivalence and empty-class lemmas, unpacked definitions, two laws of directed suprema, the hull's idempotence (its case of runs is Horizon's `Adheres.adheres`) and the classification of the ideals of words (whose process form is `Stretches.classification`). Their 18 roots are in the apart register.
- `Stretches.not_not` and the four laws after it restate Horizon's statements on purpose: they derive them from the laws of points, which is the connection. Horizon's own proofs stand.
- `closed_iff_within_lower` was re-proved through the content of the reading's runs (`Ideals.content_lower`), so its lower set is that content.
- The first scratch build of `Stretches` reported two unused variables, which the checker counts as warnings. Renamed `_`, the next build was clean, every axiom report empty.
- The A4-L board row counted 41 correspondence declarations with empty reports; the checker's list and the audit have 40.

## 190. Which links a closure needs (K1)

```text
Result(s): which-links-a-closure-needs (new); growth-constrained-fragmentation restated through it
Delta: GrownFragmentation showed, for one eight-position chain and one branched body, that each tree
       cut is certified and splits the body, and that one added retention bond lets the middle cut
       leave the chain connected (bypass_survives_cut, bypass_really_connects): examples computed by
       the kernel. Here the laws they are cases of, for any relation on any formations: removing
       links changes no closure exactly where every removed link is bypassed; the closure after
       joining one link; attaching a formation that takes part in no link changes no closure among
       the others; every link of a relation grown by attachment is listed once and separates its
       ends when cut; after one more link is joined, cutting a grown link changes no closure exactly
       where the joined link's ends lie on its two sides. On the base, a system needs a condition
       exactly where those taking part in it lie in one system only through it; a condition two
       formations take part in joins their systems as one link would. In the periphery, division keeps the bonds
       grown by attachment whatever the word, so every bond of every body grown by division
       separates its ends, and the reinforced chain's bypass is a case of the join law
Supplied premises / correspondence: none in the core; in the periphery, the model's division,
       aggregation and cut, and the bonds read both ways as the listed links
Evidence: Becoming.Cuts, 24 theorems, 31 declarations, empty axiom reports; core receipt
          `20261019T052230.247441Z`;
          PreparationCorrespondence's new section, 13 declarations with standard axioms only,
          receipt `20261019T052332.277017Z`; connectivity check passes, 478 apart of 9,919, 12 in
          Becoming.Cuts (the laws of growth by a list of attachments, roots registered as general
          structure)
Boundary: which links form or are cut, and when; how much a cut or join takes; what the parts do
          afterwards; counts of links or formations; cut returns, which stay the supplied rule's
```

Ren, 19 October 2026, after asking of `GrownFragmentation`'s three bypass theorems "why these numbers? is this really a proof?" and which of the module's theorems are general laws: "let's make these limited, non general laws, into general ones". The AI's answer to the first question: the theorems are kernel-checked proofs, but of one hand-built body (seven divisions from one position, a path of eight, the middle bond `(3,4)`, the end bond `(0,7)` joined), with the law behind them unstated. The answer to the second: of the module's 31 theorems, 14 hold for every input, and those are bookkeeping of the model's own steps, the correctness of its bounded search and rewrites of the supplied return; the two laws taken into the core on 15 October (`closure_iff_certified`, `not_within_of_closed`) and `Readout.no_judge_of_merged` are the general part; every claim about the bodies (every tree cut certified, the bypass, the cut that spends without fragmenting) was an example.

**The question.** What do the examples show in general? When does removing a link change a closure, what does joining a link add, and what about growth makes every link needed?

**The move.** Read the bonds as a relation among formations and the components as closures (`WithinClosure`, `Becoming.Feedback`). A cut is a relation with some links removed, a join a relation with one link added; growth by attachment is a list of links each of which brings in a formation that took part in no earlier link. Nothing is decided: a removed link is described by a relation `added` with `rel ∪ added` the relation before the cut, so no equality of links needs deciding.

**What is proved** (`Becoming.Cuts`).
- **A cut changes no closure exactly where every removed link is bypassed** (`Cuts.Joined`, `Cuts.closure_unchanged_iff_bypassed`): for any relation `rel` and links `added`, every closure under `rel` with `added` joined is the closure under `rel` exactly where each link of `added` has its second end within its first end's closure under `rel`. For one link read both ways (`Cuts.Link`), this is that each end lies within the other's closure (`Cuts.link_cut_unchanged_iff`), and under a symmetric relation that one does (`Cuts.link_cut_unchanged_iff_of_symm`). Relations with the same links have the same closures (`Cuts.within_congr`).
- **Joining one link** (`Cuts.within_link_iff`): after a link between `a` and `b` is joined, `g` lies within `f`'s closure exactly where it did, or `f` reaches `a` and `b` reaches `g`, or `f` reaches `b` and `a` reaches `g`. The proof certifies the right side as a closed region holding `f`, with no symmetry and no decision.
- **Attaching an unlinked formation** (`Cuts.Unlinked`, `Cuts.within_of_unlinked`, `Cuts.not_within_unlinked`, `Cuts.within_attached_iff`): a formation that takes part in no link reaches only itself and is reached by nothing else, so attaching it by one link changes no closure among the other formations.
- **Every link grown by attachment is needed** (`Cuts.Links`, `Cuts.links_symm`, `Cuts.links_split`, `Cuts.links_of_mem`, `Cuts.Attaches`, `Cuts.Attaches.suffix`, `Cuts.Attaches.listed_once`, `Cuts.attached_link_separates`): in a list of links each attaching, to another formation, one that took part in no earlier link, each link is listed once, and removing any one leaves its ends apart, whatever came before or after it. The proof goes down the links attached later: each attaches a formation other than the cut link's ends, which by the attachment law changes no closure between them.
- **After one join, a grown link is bypassed exactly where the join crosses it** (`Cuts.joined_bypass_iff`, `Cuts.joined_cut_unchanged_iff`): with one more link joined between `a` and `b`, the ends `p`, `n` of a grown link are joined without it exactly where `p` reaches one of `a`, `b` and the other reaches `n` without it; and cutting the grown link then changes no closure exactly there.

**On the base** (`Becoming.Cuts`, namespace `Flow`). A formation's system is its closure under sharing a condition (`Flow.WithinSystem`, `Becoming.Feedback`), so the laws above read on the world's own relation.
- Sharing a condition is sharing one other than `c`, or both taking part in `c` (`Flow.SharesBeside`, `Flow.BothTakePart`, `Flow.shares_iff_beside`); splitting the two needs equality of conditions decided, given as `[DecidableEq C]`.
- **Which conditions a system needs** (`Flow.system_unchanged_without_iff`): every system is what it is through the other conditions alone exactly where any two formations taking part in `c` lie in one system through the other conditions. A condition only one formation takes part in is needed by no system (`Flow.system_unchanged_of_single`).
- **A condition two formations take part in** (`Flow.withinSystem_two_takers_iff`): where exactly `a` and `b` take part in `c`, `g` lies within `f`'s system exactly where it does through the other conditions, or `f` reaches one of them and the other reaches `g` through the other conditions. The reflexive pairs `c` adds change nothing (`Cuts.within_of_steps`).
- **Alone without its only condition** (`Flow.alone_beside_of_only`, `Flow.withinSystem_of_no_part`): a formation that takes part only in `c` reaches nothing else through the other conditions and nothing reaches it; one that takes part in no condition has only itself in its system.

**In the periphery** (`PreparationCorrespondence`, new section).
- The bonds read both ways are the listed links (`adjacent_iff_links`), so being connected is lying within their closure (`connected_iff_links`).
- A division attaches the new position by at most one bond, and every bond joins positions below the count (`AttachedBelow`, `divide_attached`), so whatever the division word, the bonds stay grown by attachment (`develop_attached`, `initial_attached`). Cutting a bond grown by attachment removes exactly it (`cut_attached`).
- So every bond of every body grown by division separates its ends when cut (`bond_cut_separates`, `every_grown_bond_separates`): the general form of `every_tree_cut_certified`, for every word rather than two.
- After one aggregation, cutting a grown bond changes no connection exactly where the aggregated bond's ends lie on its two sides (`aggregate_cut_unchanged_iff`), and the reinforced chain is a case: cutting `(3,4)` after joining `(0,7)` changes no connection, `0` lying on `3`'s side and `7` on `4`'s (`reinforced_cut_unchanged`). This is the general form of `bypass_survives_cut` and `bypass_really_connects`; the two sides are still computed for the chain.

**What this changes.** The example theorems become cases: a body grown only by division is a tree, every one of its bonds needed, and a single added bond makes exactly the bonds it crosses unneeded, which is why the reinforced chain's middle cut spends without fragmenting. The ranking and summary results keep their status: `no_parent_summary_predictor` already rests on `Readout.no_judge_of_merged`, and `oldest_cut_reverses_ranking` stays a counterexample showing that the ranking of the two bodies depends on the cut law. The computed pools, kinds and returns (`central_cut_pools`, `only_equal_tree_cuts`, `central_seed_properties`, `all_cut_returns`, `uniform_cut_returns`) are evaluations of the supplied rules on the two bodies and have no law beyond those rules.

*Reading* [AI reading, open]. A link is needed by a closure exactly where nothing else carries what it carries. Growth by attachment alone makes every link needed: such a whole holds together only through each of its links, and loses a part with any one of them. A link that closes a loop is what lets a whole lose a link and keep its closures; it makes needless exactly the links on the loop it closes. Whether keeping, cutting or adding links supports 生生 is not decided here.

**Not done.** Growth by attachment read on the base (a world in which each new formation takes part only in a condition shared with one earlier formation), so that the twelve laws of growth by a list of attachments stand on the base rather than apart; which links form or are cut, and when; what a cut or join takes (the model's budget stays a supplied law); several joins at once, beyond applying `Cuts.within_link_iff` repeatedly; counts (a grown relation's links one fewer than its formations); a general law for the cut returns; an independent review.

**Self-review.** The statements were read against the Lean.
- `Cuts.closure_unchanged_iff_bypassed` certifies `WithinClosure rel f` as a region closed under the joined relation; the other direction is `WithinClosure.mono`.
- `Cuts.within_link_iff` certifies the three-way disjunction as closed under the joined relation; the link's two readings each move one disjunct to another, and `subst` is the only rewriting.
- `Cuts.within_of_unlinked` and `Cuts.not_within_unlinked` certify the regions `x = n` and `x ≠ n`; `Cuts.within_attached_iff` needs no premise `p ≠ n`.
- `Cuts.attached_link_separates` recurses on the later links; `Cuts.Attaches.listed_once` uses the same recursion with `List.Mem`'s two cases. All by structural recursion and `match`, so every declaration has an empty axiom report.
- The periphery section uses `simp`, `omega` and `List.append_of_mem`, so its theorems report `propext`, `Quot.sound` and in places `Classical.choice`; `AttachedBelow` and `initial_attached` have empty reports and are added to the checker's `EMPTY` list.
- `Flow.shares_iff_beside` decides `d = c` with the given `DecidableEq C` (a `dite`, no axiom); `Flow.withinSystem_two_takers_iff` sends each sharing through `c` to the link or to `WithinClosure.refl` by cases on the takers.
- The first connectivity measure found all 17 laws of the first draft apart: stated on any relation, used by nothing on the base. The base laws above were added so that the cut, join and attachment laws are read on the world's systems; twelve of the 24 stand on the base or are used there, and the three apart roots (the list-growth laws) are registered with their reason.
- Checker runs: core `20261019T052230.247441Z` passed (24 theorems, 31 declarations, empty reports; 263 core modules, 9,919 theorems); instance `20261019T052332.277017Z` passed (24 theorems, standard axioms only). Two earlier core runs and two instance runs, on drafts before the base laws, are not landed.

## 191. Growth by attachment on the base (K2)

```text
Result(s): which-links-a-closure-needs (restated: its laws of growth by attachment read on the base)
Delta: §190 stated the laws of growth by attachment only for lists of links (Cuts.Links,

       apart from it. Here they are read on the world's own relation: in a world grown by
       attachment, where each new formation takes part only in a condition exactly one earlier
       formation also takes part in, the systems are the closures of the grown links; every grown
       condition is attached at one place and is needed (its two takers lie in one system, and apart
       without it); the latest formation is alone without its condition; what grew up to any stage
       is grown by attachment beside the later conditions; and with one more condition exactly two
       formations take part in, a grown condition is bypassed, and every system is what it is
       without it, exactly where the new condition's takers lie on its two sides
Supplied premises / correspondence: none; the list of attachments is the hypothesis Flow.GrownBy,
       and the join law takes the new condition's two takers and DecidableEq C
Evidence: Becoming.Cuts, now 51 theorems, 60 declarations, empty axiom reports; core receipt
          `20261019T054535.337999Z`; instance receipt `20261019T054706.944271Z` (PreparationCorrespondence
          rechecked on the changed Cuts.lean, unchanged); connectivity check passes, 467 apart of
          9,946, 1 in Becoming.Cuts (`Cuts.Attaches.listed_once`, registered as restating a base law)
Boundary: whether a world grew by attachment, or in which order; several added conditions at once;
          conditions with more than two takers added later; counts; what a cut or a join takes
```

Ren's words behind this item are §190's: "let's make these limited, non general laws, into general ones" (19 October 2026; provenance, not warrant). §190 left one step open: the laws of growth by a list of attachments were general in the relation but stated on lists of links, which the base does not have, so the connectivity measure counted twelve of them apart.

**The question.** What is growth by attachment in a world, where formations relate only by taking part in conditions, and do §190's laws hold of it as they stand?

**The move.** A world's conditions grew by attachment where a list of entries says how (`Flow.GrownBy added es cond`): the entry `(p, n)` attaches the formation `n` to the earlier formation `p` by the condition `cond n`, in which exactly `p` and `n` take part; the pairs attach (`Cuts.Attaches`), so `n` took part in no earlier condition; every condition some formation takes part in was attached by an entry or lies in `added`; and no attached condition lies in `added`. With `added` empty this is a world grown wholly by attachment; with `added` the one condition `j`, it is such a world with one more condition. Nothing is decided about the world: the list is a hypothesis, read on `Flow.TakesPart`.

**What is proved** (`Becoming.Cuts`, namespace `Flow`).
- **The systems are the closures of the grown links** (`Flow.SharesOutside`, `Flow.GrownBy.within_outside_added_iff`): sharing a condition outside `added` has exactly the closures of the listed links. Without the condition that attached `n` to `p`, it has the closures of the other links (`Flow.GrownBy.outside_step`, `Flow.GrownBy.outside_of_link`, `Flow.GrownBy.within_outside_iff`).
- **Each grown condition is attached at one place** (`Flow.GrownBy.cond_ne`): no other entry attaches `cond n`. Its takers would be `p` and `n`, and its link would join what `Cuts.attached_link_separates` keeps apart without `(p, n)`; so this is proved from separation, not assumed.
- **Every grown condition is needed** (`Flow.GrownBy.condition_needed`, `Flow.GrownBy.every_condition_needed`): in a world grown wholly by attachment, the two takers of the condition that attached `n` to `p` lie in one system, and through the other conditions they lie apart; so for every condition some formation takes part in, no system is what it is without it.
- **What each new formation takes part in** (`Flow.GrownBy.attached_only`, `Flow.GrownBy.latest_alone`): the formation `n` attached by `(p, n)` takes part only in its own condition, in conditions attached later or in `added`; so the formation attached last is alone without its condition (`Flow.alone_beside_of_only`).
- **Every stage is grown by attachment** (`Flow.GrownBy.suffix`, from `Cuts.Attaches.suffix`): the entries before any stage grow the world, with the conditions attached later counted as added.
- **One more condition** (`Flow.within_of_two_takers`, `Flow.GrownBy.beside_iff`, `Flow.GrownBy.system_iff`, `Flow.GrownBy.bypass_iff`, `Flow.GrownBy.cut_unchanged_iff`): where exactly `a` and `b` take part in one more condition `j`, the systems are the closures of the grown links with the link between `a` and `b` joined, and without `cond n` they are the closures of the other grown links with it joined. So `p` and `n` lie in one system through the other conditions, and every system is what it is without `cond n`, exactly where `p` reaches one of `a`, `b` and the other reaches `n` through the conditions other than `cond n` and `j` (`Cuts.joined_bypass_iff`, `Cuts.joined_cut_unchanged_iff`).
- Supporting lemmas on places in a list (`Cuts.mem_split`, `Cuts.mem_widen`, `Cuts.mem_set_apart`, `Cuts.mem_append_cases`, `Cuts.mem_append_right`, `Cuts.exists_split`, `Cuts.append_cons_assoc`, `Cuts.links_mem`, `Cuts.links_of_link`, `Cuts.Attaches.distinct`), proved by structural recursion, since the prelude's `List.mem_append` and its kin report `propext`.

**What this changes.** The laws of growth by attachment are now laws of the world's systems: a world that grew only by attaching each new formation through one condition to one earlier formation holds together only through each of its conditions, and one condition added between two formations frees exactly the grown conditions whose two sides it joins. §190's list-growth theorems are used by these statements, so they no longer stand apart (connectivity on the landing tree: 478 apart of 9,919 before, 467 of 9,946 after; in `Becoming.Cuts` 12 of 24 before, 1 of 51 after, and none of the 27 new theorems). `Cuts.Attaches.listed_once` (each link grown by attachment is listed once) is used by nothing on the base: its reading on the world, that each grown condition is attached at one place, is `Flow.GrownBy.cond_ne`, which is stronger (no other entry attaches the same condition, whatever its pair) and is proved from separation; its root is registered as restating a law stated on the base.

*Reading* [AI reading, open]. Growth by attachment is a world whose every relation was formed by a new formation joining one already there. Such a whole has no slack: each condition carries the only way between its two sides. The first condition formed between two formations already related is what gives a whole a loop, and it frees exactly the conditions on that loop. Whether keeping or adding such conditions supports 生生 is not decided here.

**Not done.** Several added conditions at once (apply the join law once for each, or state the general cycle law); added conditions with more than two takers; counts (a world grown by attachment has one condition fewer than its formations that take part in any); which conditions form, and when, along a run; an independent review.

**Self-review.** The statements were read against the Lean.
- `Flow.GrownBy` names its four fields as hypotheses; no field states a conclusion of the theorems (separation, uniqueness of attachment and the systems are all proved).
- `Flow.GrownBy.cond_ne` uses the takers of `cond n` and `Cuts.Attaches.distinct` to get a link of the other entry joining `p` and `n`, then `Cuts.attached_link_separates`; it covers both orientations of that entry.
- `Flow.GrownBy.attached_only` uses `Cuts.Attaches.suffix` to reach the stage where `n` was attached, and its `Unlinked` field to exclude earlier conditions.
- `Flow.GrownBy.beside_iff` and `Flow.GrownBy.system_iff` decide `d = j` with the given `DecidableEq C` (a `dite`, no axiom); `condition_needed`, `every_condition_needed` and `latest_alone` decide nothing.
- `Flow.GrownBy.cut_unchanged_iff` goes through `Cuts.joined_cut_unchanged_iff` after rewriting both sides by `system_iff` and `beside_iff`, and translates its two-sides condition by `within_outside_iff`; `or_congr` and `and_congr` are the prelude's and add no axiom.
- Checker run: core `20261019T054535.337999Z` passed (51 theorems, 60 declarations in Becoming.Cuts, empty reports). Instance `20261019T054706.944271Z` passed (PreparationCorrespondence unchanged, standard axioms only), since it imports `Becoming.Cuts`.

**K3: the last apart theorem.** Ren, 19 October 2026, on `Cuts.Attaches.listed_once` standing apart: "please finish it". `Flow.GrownBy.cond_ne` reached a second entry attaching the condition `cond n` through the separation law for both of its orientations. Its case where the entry is `(p, n)` again is a second listing of one link, so it now goes through `Cuts.Attaches.listed_once`, and only the reversed orientation `(n, p)` through `Cuts.attached_link_separates`. No statement changed. Core receipt `20261019T055924.801141Z` passed (`Becoming.Cuts` 51 theorems, 60 declarations, empty axiom reports); the register entry for `listed_once` is removed, and the connectivity check passes with 466 of 9,946 apart, none in `Becoming.Cuts`. The instance module was rechecked on the new bytes (receipt `20261019T060100.173928Z`, unchanged statements). ## 192. The Changes on the spine (Y1)

```text
Result(s): hexagrams-on-the-spine (new)
Delta: the laws of return, merging, attraction, lumping and claims, stated by the spine for every
       world, read on the world the 周易 describes: six two-valued lines, the change of one line, the
       law of waxing and waning (消息) and the received order. The change of one line returns every
       configuration and merges; the law of waxing and waning merges nothing, so every configuration
       returns, the twelve 消息 hexagrams being one orbit; where only a broken line enters, everything
       is drawn into 坤; for every law of hexagrams, returning everywhere is merging nothing; the pairs
       of complements carry the law and the count of unbroken lines does not. A passage map of
       44 passages of the 易传, the classic and two commentaries, quoted from preserved
       revisions, each mapped to declarations as agreement, exact scope or divergence, and a script
       that checks the quotations, the names, the order and the chapter's table
Supplied premises / correspondence: none in the Lean; the readings of the passages are the AI's (D47)
Evidence: Becoming.Hexagrams, 71 theorems, 97 declarations, empty axiom reports; core
          receipt `20261019T060745.666273Z`; verify_mapping.py passes (44 passages, 54 fragments,
          95 declarations, the sixty-four pages of the order); connectivity check passes,
          471 apart of 10,017, 5 in Becoming.Hexagrams (the received
          order's length and pairing, roots registered as support and model witness)
Boundary: what a passage says beyond the laws; 吉凶悔吝; the images of 說卦; the reasons of 序卦;
          the relations of the places (應, 比, 中, 正); divination and number lore; collation with a
          printed edition
```

Ren, 19 October 2026, asked: “我们的work，和周易，尤其是易传之间的关系，你看得到吗，可以建立起来吗”. The AI answered with a first sorting of passages into agreement, exact scope and divergence and proposed a chapter and a module; Ren then said: “我要你把这个系统完全建立起来，要变成库的一部分，要确保它在spine上有明确的mapping” ([words](../../../../sources/15-codex-theory-conversations/2026-10-19-the-changes-on-the-spine.md)). The repository's only comparison had been one row of [the chapter on 道](../../../../theories/becoming/chapters/DAO-AND-GENERATIVITY.md) on 《系辞上》 chapter 5, written on 6 October 2026, before the spine.

**The question.** Which passages of the 易传 state structure the spine proves laws of, where does the spine give a passage its exact scope, and where do they part? And can the correspondence be checked rather than asserted?

**The move.** State the text's own structure as a world of the pure core, so that the spine's laws are checked on it rather than said of it. A hexagram is six Bools read from the bottom. Equality and membership are told by Bool functions with soundness lemmas (`eqb`, `eq_of_eqb`, `mem_of_memb`), and every match is exhaustive and non-overlapping, so no `propext` enters a source declaration. The received order is a literal generated from the preserved pages, each entry the lower and upper trigram its page names. Then quote each passage from a fixed revision, map it to the declarations it corresponds to, and check the map by script.

**What is proved** (`Becoming.Hexagrams`).
- **Configurations and the order.** The order has sixty-four entries and holds every configuration (`order_length`, `mem_order`); each pair is turned over or, where turning over gives the same hexagram, changed in every line (`order_paired`), as 孔穎達 said: 二二相耦，非覆即變.
- **The change of a line** (`changes`). Every configuration returns and can be had from every other (`changes_returns`, `reach_every`); every possibility is kept and the process merges (`changes_keeps`, `changes_merges`), a case of `Becoming.Branching`'s point that returning does not give merging nothing where the course branches.
- **Waxing and waning** (`waxWane`). It merges nothing (`waxWane_lossless`), so by `Law.lossless_iff_returns` on the order every configuration returns (`waxWane_returns`). Six steps give the complement and twelve the configuration again (`six_steps`, `twelve_steps`). From 坤 the unbroken lines rise to 乾, and from 乾 the broken lines rise to 坤 (`waxing`, `waning`); 坤 first returns at the twelfth step (`first_return`), 復 follows 乾 at the seventh step (`seventh_step`), and 隨 returns at the fourth and not the second (`fourth_step`).
- **Merging** (`wane`). Where only a broken line enters, the law merges (`wane_merges`), everything is 坤 after six steps (`wane_six`), 坤 is absorbing (`allBroken_absorbing`), and every other configuration is drawn in, never comes back, never returns, and a possibility is lost (`wane_drawn`, `wane_never_back`, `wane_not_returns`, `wane_loses`). For every law of hexagrams, every configuration returns exactly where the law merges nothing (`every_returns_iff`).
- **Symmetry and lumping.** The law commutes with the complement and turning over runs it backward (`waxWane_complement`, `reverse_waxWane`); the pairs of complements are a lumping it goes alike across, the count of unbroken lines is not: 泰 and 否 both have three, and their next configurations have four and two (`pairs_goAlike`, `yang_not_goAlike`).
- **Claims.** Along every run, a line comes to be unbroken and ceases to be at arbitrarily late steps (`arising_recurs`; `ceasing_recurs` by `Frame.claims_recur_iff`), and read as a world the places arise and cease so (`world_arising_recurs`, `world_ceasing_recurs`).
- **Going on.** Every run of every process on hexagrams revisits among its first sixty-five configurations (`revisits_within_order`); the law with its history kept is held by no list (`kept_history_unlisted`).

**The passage map.** [passages.json](development/y1-changes/passages.json) lists 44 passages: 24 agreements, 14 exact scopes, 6 divergences. [verify_mapping.py](development/y1-changes/verify_mapping.py) checks that the preserved pages have the bytes their [provenance](../../../../sources/zhouyi-yizhuan/PROVENANCE.json) binds; that every fragment occurs verbatim in its revision with Wikisource's markup removed; that every declaration is in the receipt's audited list; that the order's entries are the trigrams of the sixty-four pages, page by page and link by link; that the names given to configurations (`rising`, `falling`, `sui`) and the orbits of 乾 and 隨 are right; and that [the chapter's](../../../../theories/becoming/chapters/YI-ZHUAN-AND-BECOMING.md) table is the one the map prints.

**What this changes.** The relation of the 易传 to the theory is a checked part of the library. 无往不復 and 日新 are two readings of one law, the configurations returning and the kept history never. 窮則變 is not a law. 一陰一陽, asserted of every world without decidedness, is exactly excluded middle (`World.law_iff_em`). 象 and 易簡 have an exact scope: a reading carries the law exactly where the law goes alike across it. 感 is coupling, and the first sight of 幾 is possible only for what couples in (`Web.break_not_bounded`). 生生之謂易 is a scope, change being wider than 生生. The divergences stay: 繼之者善, 天地之大德曰生 and 天地之心 assert of the dynamics what the theory gives only under the continuation condition, and the ranks of 天尊地卑 are not in the structure. The 6 October row on 《系辞上》 points to the chapter. The connectivity measure's component counts in chapter §8.2 were stale; on this tree there are 59 components, 25 spine theorems outside the main one, none of them in `Becoming.Hexagrams`, and 161 statements on both families.

*Reading* [AI reading, D47]. The 周易 describes a world of the spine, and much of what the 易传 says of change is a law of that world: return where nothing merges, waxing and waning as one law, readings that carry the law and readings that do not, sensing as coupling. Where the 易传 speaks universally, the spine often says where the sentence holds, and that is where most of the exactness lies. Where the 易传 says the course of heaven and earth is good, the theory says it under a stated condition, or does not say it.

**Not done.** The relations of the places (應, 比, 中, 正) as indexed readings in context; the order's own reasons (序卦), of which only the pairing is checked; the judgments of fortune and the images of 說卦; the readings of 王弼, 程頤 and 朱熹 compared passage by passage; collation with a printed edition; an independent review.

**Self-review.** The statements were read against the Lean; each passage was read in its chapter of the preserved revision, each reading against what its declarations state, and every reading that goes beyond them says so in the table.

## 207. The Chinese sources on the spine (RO)

```text
Result(s): chinese-sources-on-the-spine (new)
Delta: a checked passage map of 248 passages of nine parts of Chinese thought (the 易传 beyond Y1–Y4, the 老子 with
       three commentaries and the excavated witnesses, the 儒家 line, the script with 止戈, 庄子 and 玄学, 墨辩 and
       名家, 兵家, 法家, 管子 and 纵横, the Buddhist lines received in China, others), each quoted verbatim from a
       preserved text and tied to declarations and records as agreement (95), exact scope (94) or divergence (59);
       the thesis that these lines continue one relational ontology, tested: it holds for what they start from and
       observe, their universal forms mostly need a scope, and four non-relational overlays recur, each answered
       inside its own tradition; seven gaps stated exactly
Supplied premises / correspondence: none, and no Lean; the readings are the AI's (D54); the atlases' mechanisms and
       bridges are editorial and no passage rests on them
Evidence: verify_ro.py passes (248 passages, 486 fragments, 487 declarations in receipt `20261019T130853.816105Z`, 117
          records, 527 atlas ids in an excerpt rebuilt from the two archives, the chapter's tables); 93 files
          bound by SHA-256 in sources/chinese-classical-texts/
Boundary: what a passage says beyond the laws; the truth of any passage and its authors' meaning; collation with
          printed editions and with the plates of the excavated manuscripts; an independent review
```

Ren, 19 October 2026, shared the 易道体系图 v1.3.0 that Codex had built for him and wrote: “整个中国思想的源头，道家，易经，以及整个文字符号系统，包括武（止戈 ），和一些其他的理论体系中，例如儒家，也延续了这一套“relational ontology”，因此，我希望你好好阅读，把两者之间的关系map出来，可以用sub agents，然后再体系性的整合进我们的理论” ([words](../../../../sources/15-codex-theory-conversations/2026-10-19-relational-ontology-of-chinese-thought.md)). The repository held the passage map of the 易传 (Y1–Y4) and four Chinese chapters written on 6–7 October 2026, before the spine: [道与生成](../../../../theories/becoming/chapters/DAO-AND-GENERATIVITY.md), [汉字与理论树](../../../../theories/becoming/chapters/HANZI-AND-THEORY-TREE.md), [先秦与文言](../../../../theories/becoming/chapters/PRE-QIN-AND-WENYAN.md) and [王阳明](../../../../theories/becoming/chapters/WANG-YANGMING.md).

**The question.** Do the lines Ren names, the 道家, the 易, the script with 武 and 止戈, the 儒家 and others, continue one relational ontology? Where exactly do they meet the theory, where does the spine give their sentences a scope, and where do they part?

**The move.** Read two atlases built with Codex, 周易易传与道德经体系图 v1.3.0 and 观其会通 中国传统思想研究图谱 v9.1, from their archives, bound by SHA-256. Five mappers (Opus subagents) each took a part and wrote entries in the form of the Y1 map: verbatim fragments with locator and layer, the kind, declarations, records, atlas ids, the relational structure, a reading, and gaps checked absent. The integrator built the map ([build_passages.py](development/ro-relational-sources/build_passages.py)), preserved the cited texts (93 files: archive members of the two atlases, and Wikisource pages fetched for texts the atlases lack), checked every fragment, declaration, record and atlas id, read every reading, and wrote [verify_ro.py](development/ro-relational-sources/verify_ro.py) to keep the map, the texts and [the chapter's](../../../../theories/becoming/chapters/CHINESE-SOURCES-AND-BECOMING.md) tables in agreement. "Relational" was tested by the method's requirement, with four kinds of non-relational strand named in advance: a prior ground, a nature or value fixed before relations, a will or a single centre, and a contest or rank.

**What was found.**
- *The start.* Each line has a relational root with a law on the spine: 有无相生 and 生而不有，为而不恃，长而不宰 (a move formed by the part's own policy, the difference belonging to the joint activity, no relation of possession); 仁者人也, read by 郑玄 as the 人 of 相人偶; 荀子's 名无固宜 and 求而无度量分界则不能不争 (the joint-excess law and its converse); 戴震's 理也者，情之不爽失也 (a lumping right exactly where what it lumps goes alike); 彼出于是，是亦因彼; the 墨经's 小故, which is dependence word for word; 此有故彼有，此无故彼无; the 华严's 六相. The roots are spread across 道, 儒, 墨, 名 and 佛.
- *Scope.* Exact scopes nearly equal agreements (94 to 95). The texts state relations as universal maxims, and the spine says where they hold: the 大学's 其本乱而末治者否矣 holds and 身修而后家齐 fails in general; 惠施's 氾爱万物 holds under a common feeding condition; 知彼知己，百战不殆 holds within the coupling closure; 为道日损 has a floor at the coarsest lumping that carries the law.
- *The overlays.* A prior ground (老子 25, 王弼's 以无为本, 韩康伯, 孔颖达's 元气, 朱熹's 理先气后, the 坛经's 自性, 唯识's 无境); a nature or value fixed before relations (性善, 性恶, 性即理, 君子 and 小人 fixed on the two values, 嵇康's 五声有善恶); a will or a single centre (天志, 董仲舒's 天意, 王 as 天下所归往, 一君二民); a contest or rank (不战而屈人之兵, 二柄, 民弱国强, 贵贱有等, 剛決柔). Each is answered inside its own tradition: 天行有常, 牛山, 戴震 on 理, 王夫之's 乾坤并建, 裴頠 against 郭象, the 坛经's 一念绝即死, 法藏's 仍體不同.
- *Two senses of relational.* The 兵家, 法家, 管子 and 鬼谷子 read situations relationally and direct the reading at one standpoint's advantage; divergences are densest there (8 of 13).
- *The script.* Relational as a system of readings: 形声 pairs two coarse readings, 假借 is resolved across uses, 部首 is a lumping, a phonetic is an installed encoding, 阙如 is silence where the evidence merges cases. The graphs do not encode a relational ontology: most pair a category and a sound, and the most cosmological analyses (王 參通, 始一终亥) are centred. A controlled single-character term is a stipulation, not a recovered sense.
- *武 and 止戈.* Two layers kept apart: 止 is a foot, and the 說文 itself glosses it so; 止戈 is 楚庄王's reading in the 左传. His speech evaluates force by what it does to the loop of force, tests it by seven guards, counts both sides' dead, refuses gain at another's juncture, and sees that nothing settles while 晉 stands (`Law.aboveAll_never_rests`); its frame is a contest for standing (保大, 定功, 示子孙, the 京观 kept for the 不敬).

**Corrections.** Six, each with its reason in the map: four quotations (郑玄's note as it stands in 禮記正義 卷五十二; 程頤's preface from the 四庫 page; the quotation marks of the 說文 gloss of 武; 惠施's 无), and two readings: the 老子's first chapter had been called a theorem, and is now isomorphic to the diagonal theorems under a reading; 河上公 on chapter 39 had "the theory supports chapter 39", and now says which laws agree with which chapter.

**Gaps.** Seven, each checked absent by name, docstring and record digest: two-sided regulation of a level and its late-reading form (人之道, 冲气以为和, 宽猛相济); a code formed between formations (约定俗成, with readings written back into their own evidence); capture through the rule (二柄, 据有余而制不足); a graded order by closure level (差等); division across several conditions (人何以能群？曰：分); tolerance compared across laws (柔弱者生之徒); and the hexagram world's order, exchange, parity and 雜卦 (the received order is a run of no three-cell local rule and of no law permuting the places and applying a mask, computed by script, not yet in Lean). Relative position was closed during the mapping (Z1, `Becoming.RelativePosition`); simultaneous mutual support (因果俱时, 芦束互依) belongs to MD1.

**What this changes.** The relation of Chinese thought to the theory is a checked part of the library, with the divergences visible so that the texts can test the theory. The earlier chapters keep their scope; their role as the entry point for the Chinese sources passes to the new chapter, whose §9 says for each what it keeps, extends and supersedes. Chapter §1 gains a paragraph, §8.3 an item and §11 a row; the four earlier chapters point to the new one.

*Reading* [AI reading, D54]. One relational ontology is a dominant thread in these lines and a position within each, not every system's doctrine or the commentaries' consensus. Where the texts start and observe, they read the relation first; where they measure and ground, they often do not; and the answer to each non-relational overlay is already inside the tradition that has it.

**Not done.** The seven gaps; passages the mappers listed for a later pass; the role-bound strata (ritual detail, the 孝经, the judgments of the 春秋, the 老子's governance chapters), which the selection under-represents; collation with printed editions and with the plates of the 郭店 and 帛书 manuscripts; moving the superseded parts of the earlier chapters to history; an independent review.

**Self-review.** Every Lean name a reading mentions was checked to exist; the agreements of every part were read for overclaims, and the divergences for whether they assert a verdict where the theory has only its condition. Each mapper's counter-review is kept in its notes ([development/ro-relational-sources/mappers/](development/ro-relational-sources/mappers/)) and in the readings it qualified.

**The earlier chapters (RH, 19 October 2026).** The four earlier Chinese chapters were read passage by passage against the map and the spine. Each 6–7 October text moved byte for byte to `theories/becoming/history/` with the move tool, inbound links kept on the live path (batch `RH-chinese-chapters`, receipt `_process/architecture/moves/RH-chinese-chapters.json`). At each path a live chapter keeps, in current terms, what neither the map nor the spine carries, and ends with a table of where each original section went. [道与生成](../../../../theories/becoming/chapters/DAO-AND-GENERATIVITY.md) keeps the four judgments in “explicating 道” with their present answers, the readings of 德 and 无为, the modern interpretations and the passages the map lacks; its argument from generation to the good goes to chapter sections 5 and 6 and G0-WARRANT. [汉字与理论树](../../../../theories/becoming/chapters/HANZI-AND-THEORY-TREE.md) keeps its method under its original section numbers: four kinds of correspondence, compounds, acceptance criteria and relation markers. Its 武 gloss goes to the new chapter's §6, its vocabulary table to the naming study. [先秦与文言](../../../../theories/becoming/chapters/PRE-QIN-AND-WENYAN.md) keeps 察今, now stated through `Pace` and `Clearing.pool_closes_gap` rather than a right to revise rules, and other findings the map lacks: 管子 内业, how concern forms, the same-word counterexamples, later wenyan, the 维摩经 and genre. [王阳明](../../../../theories/becoming/chapters/WANG-YANGMING.md) keeps its reading of the whole under its original section numbers, and its formal entry through the periphery module `SituatedPractice` is superseded. One point was missing: the new chapter's 心外无理 row sends the sense of 理 in conduct to that chapter, which had not stated it. It now does, quoting 徐爱's record from the preserved 传习录 (`S10.txt`): 孝's 理 is not sought on the father but in how this mind responds in serving him. No reading changed status. No Lean was written and no checker was run.

## 193. What a collective's continuation needs (V)

```text
Result(s): giving-that-waits-on-giving, whether-a-loop-closes-a-difference, how-fast-a-rule-may-change,
           a-pattern-lasts-through-passing, conditions-kept-together (all new); reused:
           recurrence-without-premise, how-often-couplings-act, target-capture, identification-where-bounded,
           whole-persists-through-generation, becoming-renewal-reading, finite-continuation-plans,
           where-a-run-goes-on
Delta: five core modules closing the four gaps an eight-constraint account of social viability exposed
       (cooperation among strangers, bounded conflict, stability with adaptability, forming the next
       members) and carrying two of its five pushbacks as laws (conditions joined, not multiplied;
       keeping a part is not renewal). Withholding: with memory, withholding absorbs; without
       memory it passes out where no chain is long enough and returns around a loop; restoring needs
       another law. Widening: a loop closes a difference only through a link that gives back less
       than it received; whole-number strengths close at once, keep or run away. Pace: a fixed rule
       loses what it merges; a stretch fixes the held course exactly when it is at least 2N - 1 steps.
       Passing: a pattern of brief carriers lasts only through passing; one empty step ends it.
       JointKeeping: conditions decompose exactly under every course and not along some course; no
       rule on the separate keepabilities decides the joint one; keeping a part decides neither
       renewal nor what the run does to others
Supplied premises / correspondence: none in the Lean beyond each law's hypotheses; the passing
       premise (Web.ByPassing) is a hypothesis; the readings of the eight constraints are the AI's (D48)
Evidence: Becoming.Withholding (38 theorems), Becoming.Widening (46), Becoming.Pace (31),
          Becoming.Passing (19), Becoming.JointKeeping (23); 157 theorems, empty axiom reports; core
          receipt `20261019T064004.300228Z`; connectivity check passes, 469 apart of 10,174, none in the five modules; Law.lost_stays, registered
          apart as restating, is now used on the base (Becoming.Pace) and leaves the register
Boundary: amounts of giving and thresholds of waiting; real strengths and a loop closing gradually by
          a multiplication below one; many levels and noisy rules; passing derived from descent; the
          named readings (homeostasis, carrying capacity, fault tolerance) as instance theorems
```

Ren, 19 October 2026, pasted an account of social viability: eight constraints whose long and systematic violation ends a society's capacity to maintain itself, a ninth unifying them (keeping the capacity to correct), a product formula `Viability = Perception × Coordination × Correction × Regeneration`, and the proposal that these are viability invariants of every complex adaptive system, from which a small set of "system survival axioms" might be distilled. He asked: "does our theories fully cover this?" ([words](../../../../sources/15-codex-theory-conversations/2026-10-19-collective-continuation.md)). The AI's mapping found constraints 1–3 and 6 and the correction point carried by spine laws, constraints 4, 5, 7 and 8 partial or missing, and five pushbacks: survival of "a society" is not the measure; there is no number of the whole; the product is a heuristic; checks and balances are not the starting point; the invariants are theorems, not axioms. Ren: "please, spawn a swarm of subagents, think hard, let's fully complete this", and, while the work ran, "I agree with your push back, let's think about how to resolve them elegantly". His agreement is provenance; each pushback stands on its law.

**The question.** For each missing constraint, what law of one unfolding states it, under which local conditions, and where is its limit? And can a pushback be carried by a law rather than a disclaimer?

**The move.** Each constraint is stated on runs of the spine (`Law.run`, `Run`, `Viability.Kernel`) or on a web, so that it is a law of courses, not of a society as a unit. The brief ([BRIEF.md](../history/root-foundation/development/v-collective-continuation/BRIEF.md)) fixed the statements; five Opus provers built the modules in scratch, each reviewed by an independent Opus reviewer against the brief (exactness, docstring claims, reuse, the connectivity base, vocabulary), and blocking findings were fixed before landing. Two review findings changed the brief: a `Law.orbit` course alone is not the connectivity base (the measure counts `Run`/`Process` and `World`/`Flow`/`Web`), so every main law is stated on `Law.run`, whose states are the orbit by `rfl`; and laws already proved elsewhere were cited instead of reproved (`Lasting.Variant.reaches`, `Lasting.orbit_mono`, `IdentificationRuns.statesBelow_congr`, prelude `iff_of_true`, `eq_false_of_ne_true`).

**What is proved.**

- **Withholding** (constraint 4, cooperation among strangers). Formations and a relation of waiting, `up b a`: the giving of `a` waits on that of `b`. With memory (`waitsAll`: a formation gives where it gave and all it waits on gave), a formation gives at step `n` exactly where every formation within `n` waits of it gave at the start (`waitsAll_closed`); withholding stays (`waitsAll_withholding_stays`) and spreads downstream (`withholding_spreads`), and one withholding ends all giving in a family reached from it within `d` waits from step `d` on (`withholding_absorbs`). Without memory (`answers`: a formation gives where all it waits on gave the step before), the closed form counts chains of exactly `n` waits (`answers_closed`); where no chain of `L` waits exists, every formation gives from step `L` on whatever the start (`gives_without_chain`, exact in `Line`); on a loop of `p` waits, withholding returns at every multiple of `p` (`withholding_returns`). More waiting is less giving under both laws (`waitsAll_more_waiting`, `answers_more_waiting`). In `Ring`, three formations each waiting on the one before: with memory all withhold from step 2, exactly; without memory the withholding circulates; under the law in which one formation gives whatever it waits on (`givesFirst`), every formation gives from step 3 on from every start, exactly (`Ring.givesFirst_restores`, `Ring.givesFirst_restores_exact`).
- **Widening** (constraint 5, bounded conflict; and the open item of §7.7, which law closes rather than widens a difference). On runs of a return map `f : Nat → Nat`: where every link gives on at least what it receives, the difference never falls below where it began (`never_closes_of_no_less`), so a loop that closes a positive difference has a link giving back less than it received, found (`closing_needs_less`). A return map below what it receives at every positive difference closes within `d` turns, exactly (`closes_within`, an instance of `Lasting.Variant.reaches`; `closes_within_exact`), and a closing loop merges two differences (`closing_merges`), so it is not lossless. Taking a constant off closes at the least turn covering the difference (`orbit_sub_const`, `sub_const_closes`, `sub_const_open`). A cut closes at once where every link after it gives nothing for nothing (`cut_closes`); without that condition a link after the cut reopens it (`cut_reopened`). Monotone return maps settle within `d` turns or never fall (`settles_within`, `never_falls`). Doubling links run away (`runs_away`, exact in `doubling_exact`). With whole-number strengths a loop closes at the first turn (product `0`), keeps the difference (product `1`) or runs away (product at least `2`), nothing between (`whole_strengths`, `nothing_between`): closing gradually needs a link that is not a multiplication (`gradual_needs_another_link`).
- **Pace** (constraint 7, stability with adaptability). A two-level course, the fast configuration stepping by a rule that changes only at reading steps, is a run of one law (`paced_run`). A rule that never reads is kept, nothing the fast level meets reaches it (`rule_unreached`), and under it what is lost stays lost and merges lose configurations (`never_reads_lost`, `never_reads_loses`); a fast difference reaches the rule only at a reading step, exactly (`rule_until_reading`, `Copying.rule_parts`); regaining needs a change of rule (`Switching.fixed_loses`, `Switching.changing_regains`). Given two values, a stretch of `L` steps fixes every pair of courses with at most `N` states that held rules generate exactly when `L ≥ 2N - 1` (`pace_law`; `dissolving` from the witness of `Identification.prefix_short_twice`, `held_fixed` from `Identification.bounded_agree`); a course of configurations read whole is fixed by its first `N + 1` steps, exactly (`whole_fixed`, `whole_fixed_exact`).
- **Passing** (constraint 8, forming the next members). On a web whose activity is carrying a pattern: present from `T` on with carriers brief for `d`, a carrier begins within every `d` steps (`Web.begins_within`, an instance of `Web.Covered.arises_within`). Under the passing premise (`Web.ByPassing`, supplied, as transmission is in `Becoming.Evolution`), every beginning is a passing, the pattern is passed across one of every `d` steps (`Web.ByPassing.passes_within`), a step with no carrier is followed by none with one (`Web.ByPassing.empty_stays`), and where passing stops it ends within `d` steps (`Web.ByPassing.ends_within`). `PatternRelay` attains each bound.
- **JointKeeping** (pushbacks 1 and 3). Under every course, conditions decompose exactly (`Viability.kernel_and_iff`, `kernel_allOf_iff`). Along some course they do not: in `ChoicePoint` each of two guards is keepable from the start and the two together are not (`ChoicePoint.each_not_joint`), and for every rule on the separate keepabilities the joint one is not that rule of them (`ChoicePoint.no_rule_decides_joint`, with the decisions shown to exist, `ChoicePoint.decisions_exist`); kept for `n` steps likewise (`ChoicePoint.keptFor_each_not_joint`). In `Renewable` no course leaves the guard "the focal formation is active" from any configuration, while from one configuration one run renews and another consumes the sustaining formation's condition (`Renewable.kept_part_not_renewal`, from `Renewable.class_belongs_to_the_run`).

**The eight constraints restated.** Chapter §4, "What a collective's continuation needs", gives each constraint its law and its limit, and the five framing changes, each carried by a law: keeping a part is not renewal (`Renewable.kept_part_not_renewal`, `Becoming.Continuation`); there is no number of the whole (`Flow.act_unselected`, `Flow.favours_reaching_beyond`, and the priority of basic conditions excluding natural-number scores); conditions are joined, not multiplied (`Viability.kernel_and_iff`, `ChoicePoint.no_rule_decides_joint`); a counter-loop has to reach the rule (`Law.perturbation_reabsorbed`, pooled coupling); the invariants are laws, not axioms.

**Counter-review (the author's).** (1) *Are the new laws about societies?* No: they are laws of courses, true wherever the representation fits; the reading onto cooperation, conflict, institutions and generations is the AI's (D48), and whether an actual collective meets a law's conditions is empirical. (2) *Is `waitsAll` a fair model of trust?* It is one law of waiting, the strictest; `answers` is the forgetful one; amounts and thresholds of waiting are open. The structural point does not depend on the model's strictness: wherever giving waits on giving and a loop closes, withholding returns, and a law that gives without waiting is what restores. (3) *Does `whole_strengths` say conflicts cannot be resolved gradually?* It says a loop of whole-number multiplications cannot close gradually; compensation (`sub_const_closes`) and maps below what they receive (`closes_within`) do. Real strengths are open. (4) *Is `pace_law` about institutions?* It is about what a stretch of a held rule fixes; reading a constitution as a slow level reading the fast one is the AI's. (5) *Does JointKeeping refute the product formula?* It refutes its claim to decide joint viability from separate scores where continuation goes through choices, and confirms its "any factor zero" half under every course. (6) *Independent review*: each module was reviewed by an agent that did not write it; that is not an independent human review.

**What would change it.** A law deriving cooperation's giving from the flow rather than supplying the waiting relation; a loop law with real strengths; a collective whose continuation decomposes along choices (which would show the choice structure absent there, not refute `each_not_joint`).

## 194. Thresholds of waiting and the laws that restore giving (V2)

```text
Result(s): restoring-giving-from-the-worst-start, thresholds-of-waiting (both new); reused:
           giving-that-waits-on-giving, recurrence-without-premise; the certificate laws of
           Becoming.FaultEnvelopes (no record of their own)
Delta: V's Withholding showed restoring needs another law, in one ring. Here the general family:
       for every law keeping inclusion, restoring from every start is restoring from total
       withholding, giving from it only grows, and restoring needs a formation giving after it;
       under givesFirst with decided sources restoring by step n is exactly no clear chain of n
       waits. Thresholds of waiting (the tolerating law, giving where all but tol a of what a
       formation waits on gave) keep a set giving that relies on at most its tolerance outside
       it and absorb a thin withholding in one step, and restore nothing without a formation
       sparing all it waits on. The certificate of FaultEnvelopes is read as a law of giving
Supplied premises / correspondence: none in the Lean beyond each law's hypotheses; the decision
       of which formations are sources (∀ a, src a ∨ ¬ src a) is a hypothesis of the converse of
       restores_iff only; readings onto collectives are the AI's (D48)
Evidence: Becoming.Tolerance (52 theorems, 65 declarations), empty axiom reports; core
          receipt `20261019T083316.966154Z`; connectivity check passes, 488 apart of 10,334, none in the module;
          FaultEnvelopes.availability_iff_separated and correlated_three_blocks, registered
          apart, are now used on the base and leave the register
Boundary: amounts of giving; thresholds with memory; how a law that tolerates or gives first
          forms; the remaining items of chapter §8.2 "Collective continuation" (real strengths,
          passing from descent, many levels of rule, homeostasis and carrying capacity)
```

Chapter §8.2's row "Collective continuation", after V (§193), left open amounts of giving and thresholds of waiting, which laws that give first restore giving in a general family, and fault tolerance as an instance joined to `Becoming.FaultEnvelopes`. This section takes the second, the thresholds, and fault tolerance in two forms (board item V2).

**The question.** `Withholding.Ring.givesFirst_restores` shows one law restoring one ring. Which laws restore giving, from which starts, by which step, in any family? And what does a formation that may go without some of what it waits on change?

**The move.** Every law of the family keeps inclusion: more giving now gives at least as much giving next (`KeepsInclusion`; `waitsAll_keeps`, `answers_keeps`, `givesFirst_keeps`, `tolerating_keeps`). For such a law the question "does `a` give at step `n` from every start" has one witness start, total withholding. No case split on the start is needed, so the laws are constructive with no decision of giving. Thresholds are counted on the list of what a formation waits on, by the inductive `AllBut s f l` (all but at most `f` members of `l` hold `s`). No count of a predicate is needed, and so no decision.

**What is proved** (`Becoming.Tolerance`, every main law on `Law.run`).

- **The worst start.** `worst_start`: `(∀ s, (Law.run next s).state n a) ↔ (Law.run next allWithheld).state n a`. `rises_from_withheld` (giving from total withholding at `n` gives giving at `n + 1`), `restored_stays` (restored by `n`, restored at every `m ≥ n` from every start), `withheld_kept` (no formation in `next allWithheld`, then none at any step).
- **Restoring under `givesFirst`, exactly.** A clear chain is a chain of waits none of whose formations after the first is a source (`Clear`). `clear_withholds`: a clear chain of `n` waits into `a` makes `a` withhold at `n` from total withholding. `restores_iff` (with sources decided): `(∀ s, state n a) ↔ ∀ b, ¬ Clear src up n b a`. `restores_from`: no clear chain of `L` waits gives giving everywhere from `L` on. `clear_loop_withholds`: a clear loop of `p + 1` waits withholds at its formation at every step from total withholding. `Ring.no_clear_three` and `Ring.restores_from_three` make V's `Ring.givesFirst_restores` an instance.
- **Thresholds.** `tolerating tol ups s a := AllBut s (tol a) (ups a)`. `tolerating_zero`: with every tolerance `0`, the course is that of `answers (Listed ups)` at every step. `gives_needs_sparing`: from total withholding a giving formation finds one with `(ups b).length ≤ tol b`; `sparing_gives`: such a formation gives at every step after the start; `total_stays`: without one, total withholding at a step is total withholding after it. `kept_set`: a set giving at the start, each member with `AllBut G (tol a) (ups a)`, gives at every step. `thin_absorbed`: the start giving outside `W` and every formation with `AllBut (¬ W ·) (tol a) (ups a)` gives giving everywhere from step 1.
- **The certificate law.** `certified roster faults s a := certificate (roster a) (faults a) s` on configurations `Domain → Bool`. `certified_kept` (from `certificate_available`), `certified_available_iff` (`availability_iff_separated`, at step 1), `certified_blocked` (`correlated_three_blocks`: without separation a withholding within an admitted fault set stops every domain at step 1).
- **Witness `Triad`**, three formations each waiting on the other two, one withholding: `Triad.spreads` (tolerance 0: all withhold from step 2, `first` still gives at step 1), `Triad.absorbed` (tolerance 1: all give from step 1, an instance of `thin_absorbed`), `Triad.total_kept` (tolerance 1 from total withholding: nothing gives, an instance of `withheld_kept`).

**Relations.** `worst_start` is the monotone counterpart of `Withholding.withholding_absorbs`: with memory, the course from total withholding is total withholding. `clear_withholds` refines `withholding_spreads`: withholding spreads along a chain unless a formation on it gives first. `thin_absorbed` is the tolerating form of `gives_without_chain`. The two laws of fault tolerance differ: the tolerating law counts what may be missing, and the certificate law lists the sets that may fail together. The first is not stated as an instance of the second: the envelope of all sets of at most `f` would need a listing of subsets, which nothing here uses.

**Counter-review (the author's).** (1) *Is `restores_iff` classical?* Only its converse uses a decision, and only of which formations are sources, a hypothesis named in the statement; the forward direction and `clear_withholds` need none. (2) *Is the worst start trivial?* Its proof is short, but it is what makes restoration a property of one course: every question "from every start" is asked of total withholding. The monotonicity it rests on holds for the whole family of V and the tolerating law. (3) *Does tolerance restore?* No (`Triad.total_kept`, `total_stays`): it absorbs a thin withholding and keeps a set that relies little outside itself, and only a formation sparing all it waits on starts giving from total withholding. (4) *Lists, not counts of predicates.* The list `ups a` fixes the multiplicity of waits; a formation waiting twice on one formation counts it twice. This is the reading of a finite roster, as in `Becoming.FaultEnvelopes`. (5) *Built in this session*, with no separate reviewer; the scratch build and the checker audit every declaration.

**Output → input.** The worst start feeds any later law of restoring in a monotone family: one course to compute. `kept_set` and `certified_kept` give the sets that keep giving, and their complements are where amounts of giving and thresholds with memory, still open, would be read.

## 195. The relations of the places in the Changes (Y2)

```text

       (adjacent lines) and 中 (the middle height), stated as readings indexed by their sites

       told by phase; the laws of the relations under the complement, turning over, the change of a line
       and the law of waxing and waning, the oppositions a lumping the law goes alike across and the
       count in phase not; every law read along the runs of the spine; 22 passages and four
       censuses of the text checked against the preserved pages

          (what the text says of named configurations and the censuses, registered as model witnesses,

Output -> input: the relations of the places as contextual readings of the hexagram world, read along its
```
