On 19 October 2026 Ren asked for the earlier repository to be read for what can be integrated ("please take a look of this … many insights can be integrated"). The [review](SSBX-REPOSITORY-REVIEW.md) found three small general laws, argued there and proved only in instances or not at all, that the spine lacked (§3.2, G1–G3): 机 as a juncture, from 补篇一 §八 and §十一 ([卷二](../../../../sources/07-shengsheng-buxi/ssbx-repo/史料/生生不息论_三本文完整版/03_补篇一_间开本_致知版/03_卷二_发生.md), [卷三](../../../../sources/07-shengsheng-buxi/ssbx-repo/史料/生生不息论_三本文完整版/03_补篇一_间开本_致知版/04_卷三_判准.md)); a commuting law never merging the pairs of a fixed-point-free symmetry, from [义理·拓扑](../../../../sources/07-shengsheng-buxi/ssbx-repo/义理/拓扑%20·%20从元到障.md) §四 and §九; and three-valued revision, from [义理·形式逻辑](../../../../sources/07-shengsheng-buxi/ssbx-repo/义理/形式逻辑%20·%20从元到推.md) §三. `Becoming.Branching` has no juncture and no keeping restriction (checked), and `Relabel.Equivariant` is a law of selection, not of a law of change. The earlier Lean for these is instance-only or absent, so each is proved again, prelude-only.

**The question.** Where, on a branching course, is a configuration lost, and what does finding that place ask? What does a law of change do with a difference a symmetry carries? What does revision of what a system says of itself do when a value may stay undecided?

**What is proved.**

- **Junctures** ([Becoming.Junctures](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/Junctures.lean)). `x` is a juncture for `s` where it has a step after which `s` can still be had and a step after which it cannot (`Juncture`). A juncture can have `s` again, its two steps differ in outcome, it is possibly drawn, and on the course of `s` it returns (`Juncture.reach`, `Juncture.outcomes_differ`, `Juncture.possiblyDrawn`, `Juncture.returns`): it is where `Branching`'s possibly and necessarily drawn come apart. Where `s` returns, every course from `s` to a configuration that cannot have `s` again passes, not not, a juncture at which the course takes its losing step (`loss_passes_juncture`, `loss_passes_juncture_from`, `PossiblyDrawn.passes_juncture`). The proof walks the course and asks at each configuration whether `s` can still be had; it needs that answer, so the claim is stated up to double negation. Where the answer is given along the course, the juncture is found (`loss_passes_juncture_decided`); for configurations a list holds with steps decided, it is given: a reading of the steps that only rises settles by the list's length (`reach_iff_leads`, `reach_decided_listed`, through `Undecided.settles_within`), and the juncture is found (`loss_passes_juncture_listed`). It cannot be given in general: if every loss of every process had its juncture found, every sequence of truth values would have a `true` or be `false` throughout (`lpo_of_junctures_found`, on the process `Hidden`, where whether `origin` can be had again from `fork` is whether a sequence has a `true`). So the double negation says what the unfolding asks: finding the juncture is deciding whether `s` can still be had again. `keeping P s` keeps the steps after which `s` can still be had and `losing P s` the others; a juncture is where both have a step (`juncture_iff`, by `Iff.rfl`). Keeping can have `s` from where `P` can, keeps `s`, returns to `s` exactly where `P` does, and holds every sub-process of `P` that keeps `s` on that sub-process's course from `s` (`reach_keeping_iff`, `keeping_keeps`, `keeping_returns_iff`, `keeping_greatest`); what it removes on its own course are the losing steps at junctures (`keeping_removes_at_juncture`). Losing never returns to `s` (`losing_not_returns`, `losing_loses`). Where `P` keeps `s` no configuration on its course is a juncture (`no_juncture_of_keeps`): `Many` has a step for every natural number at its one configuration and no juncture, while `OneWay`'s `false`, with two moves, is one (`Many.no_juncture`, `OneWay.juncture`).
- **What a commuting law keeps apart** ([Becoming.Commuting](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/Commuting.lean)). Where `T (σ x) = σ (T x)` for every `x` (`Law.Commutes`), the run of the law from `σ x` is the image of its run from `x` (`Law.Commutes.iterate`, on `Law.run`), so where `σ` moves every configuration (`Diagonal.Moves Eq σ`) the two runs are never at one configuration at the same step (`Law.Commutes.apart`); a law that merges them breaks the symmetry (`Law.Commutes.breaks`). Such a law brings no two runs to one configuration at every start, so it is not constant (`Law.Commutes.not_drawn_to_one`); a run resting at `x` has its image resting at `σ x`, and returning carries over to the image (`Law.Commutes.rest_paired`, `Law.Commutes.returns_paired`, the latter as `Branching.Returns` of the law's process); under an exchange a run holding a configuration's image `k` steps on holds every configuration's image `k` steps on and returns at `2k` (`Law.Commutes.paired_halfway`, `Law.Commutes.halfway_returns`); for every naming of the pairs, the law goes alike across them (`Law.Commutes.pairs_lumped`, `Learning.Lumped`, and as a process `Law.Commutes.pairs_goAlike`, `GoAlike`). The run from a configuration `σ` fixes stays where `σ` fixes (`Law.Commutes.keeps_fixed`): with `Relabel.Equivariant.tied`, which keeps a tie through an exchange, it is the fixed case of the structure whose free case is `apart`; the two laws do not overlap. Every map commutes with itself, so `Diagonal.revision_never_rests` is the case `T = σ` (`Law.Commutes.self_apart`). For processes, a symmetry carries reach, returning and, under an exchange, junctures, and every run has a mirror run never at the same configuration at the same step (`Branching.Symmetric.reach`, `.returns`, `.juncture`, `Branching.mirror_apart`); a commuting law is a symmetric process (`Branching.law_symmetric`). In the Changes the complement moves every hexagram (`Hexagram.complement_moves`); waxing and waning never brings a hexagram and its complement to one (`Hexagram.waxWane_apart`); its six steps to the complement are the pair halfway round the return of twelve (`Hexagram.waxWane_halfway`, which gives `twelve_steps` again); Y1's `pairs_goAlike` is the general law's instance (`Hexagram.pairs_goAlike_of_commutes`); the waning into 坤 breaks the symmetry (`Hexagram.wane_breaks`); and the change of one line is symmetric under the complement (`Hexagram.changes_symmetric`, `Hexagram.changes_mirror_apart`). 互 and the four-group of 錯 and 綜 are left to Y3 (`Becoming.HexagramLaws`), which can cite `Law.Commutes.apart`.
- **The third value and revision** ([Becoming.Undecided](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/Undecided.lean)). Values `t`, `u`, `f`, with `u` below the decided values in information (`Le`); terms built from sentences and the two decided constants by negation, conjunction and disjunction, with the strong tables, which agree with the two-valued ones on decided values (`eval_embed`). A term with no constant (`ConstantFree`) is undecided where every sentence is (`eval_undecided`), so a system with no constant stays wholly undecided at every stage (`stays_undecided`): revision decides only what a constant decides first. Evaluation is monotone in information (`eval_mono`, `eval_mono_below`). For `N` sentences that speak only of one another (`Closed`), revision from every sentence undecided (`stage`, the run `Law.run` of `revise`) rises at every step and along the run (`stage_up`, `stage_mono`) and settles within `N` steps (`settles`, `settled_from`) at the least fixed point (`stage_fixed`, `stage_le_fixed`, `least_fixed`). The bound is exact: in the chain whose first sentence says true and each next denies the one before, sentence `k` is undecided up to stage `k` and decided after, so `N + 1` sentences are steady at step `N + 1` and not at `N` (`chain_undecided`, `chain_decided`, `chain_exact`). The counting is its own law: readings on a list that only rise, and once steady stay steady, are steady by the list's length (`settles_within`); `Becoming.Junctures` uses it for reach. The liar rests undecided at every stage, and a run of its revision from any start rests exactly where it is undecided (`liar_rests`, `liar_rests_iff`, `neg_fixed_iff`); the truth-teller keeps whatever value it starts with and rests undecided from all undecided (`truthTeller_keeps`, `truthTeller_rests`). Where the two-valued revision of a closed system has no fixed point, every three-valued fixed point, and every run of the three-valued revision that rests, leaves a sentence undecided (`undecided_of_moves`, `least_undecided`, `rest_undecided`, `liar_undecided`); for the liar, the two-valued revision is the run of negation and never rests (`liar_two_valued_run`, `liar_two_valued_never_rests`, by `Diagonal.revision_never_rests`), so the liar never rests with two values and rests undecided with three (`liar_both_sides`). Three-valued negation is monotone and does not move every value (`neg_not_moves`); no monotone map does (`monotone_fixed`, `monotone_not_moves`), and the run of a monotone map from the undecided value rests from its first step (`monotone_run_rests`), so a run from the undecided value that never rests is not of a monotone map (`never_rests_not_monotone`): the gap of `Diagonal.gap_unsaid` needs a map deciding the undecided, which is not monotone (`moves_not_monotone`). A family of three-valued readings within what it reads is still incomplete (`incomplete`, by `Diagonal.fixed_of_complete` with the rotation).

**Connectivity.** The laws are stated on the base: junctures and keeping on processes and traces, the commuting laws and revision on runs of the spine (`Law.run`), and the Changes through `Law.process` and `Branching.Symmetric`. A first draft stated the commuting laws and revision on `Law.orbit` and left 57 theorems apart; restated on runs, only `Undecided.incomplete`, a law of every family of three-valued readings on any type, and the lemma it uses stand apart, and `incomplete` is registered as general structure (its run form for every map moving every value is `DiagonalRuns.incomplete`).

**Readings (the AI's, decided from the work under D45; D52).** 机 is a juncture: the earlier text's "两个延续通向不同的开放之未来", read with "open" as one configuration still to be had; its profile of openness is not formalized. 护闭 is keeping, the largest closure that keeps `s` to be had again on its course from `s`; 成闭 is losing, after which `s` never returns. Neither carries a value: which configuration is kept, and whether keeping it supports or damages 生生, goes through §6.15. Many options make no juncture, as the earlier text said (two options are needed, not sufficient). The earlier topology's "«一» structurally does not exist" and its table equating Borsuk–Ulam with the second law are not taken; what is taken is the law: to merge what a symmetry carries, a law must break it. The third value 疑 is what revision has not decided, not a third truth and not superposition (the review's guardrail "不确定 ≠ 不可知"); the earlier "三值保守律" (U ⇏ ⊤) is `eval_undecided` for terms without constants and, along the run, `stays_undecided`.

**Counter-review (the author's).** (1) *Is the juncture law a renaming of `possiblyDrawn_iff`?* No: `possiblyDrawn_iff` says a loss exists on some course; the juncture law says where on the course it happens and what finding it asks, with the LPO calibration as the boundary of the `∃` form. (2) *Is `keeping` greatest in the right sense?* A sub-process that keeps `s` may take steps anywhere off its course from `s`; `keeping_greatest` constrains exactly the steps on that course, which is what keeping `s` concerns. (3) *Is G2 trivial?* The proof is three lines; the law is that commuting is enough, with no involution, finiteness or decision, and its content is in its cases: the diagonal's rhythm, the received pairing, the waning that breaks it. (4) *Does the three-valued settling need the closure hypothesis?* Yes: a sentence speaking of sentences outside the first `N` lets their revision reach in; `Closed` names it. (5) *Is the settling empty?* Without constants it would be: every stage is wholly undecided (`stays_undecided`), the first draft's case, which the review's G3 bullet (terms without constants) states. With constants revision decides, and the chain shows that `N` steps are needed (`chain_exact`). (6) *Independent review*: none by a person; the statements were checked against the review's §3.2 bullet by bullet.

**What would change it.** A process in which every loss has a juncture found without deciding reach (it would refute `lpo_of_junctures_found`'s reading only if LPO held there); a law commuting with a fixed-point-free map that merges a pair (impossible by `apart`); a closed system whose least fixed point is decided while its two-valued revision has no fixed point (impossible by `least_undecided`).

## 200. The game of relative position (Z1)

```text
Result(s): relative-position-is-zero-sum (new)
Delta: the opening's note [^aligned] said that a game of relative position is zero-sum "is a
       matter of counting, not yet stated on the formal spine". Stated here: a part's position,
       read against the others as two counts, is zero-sum across every change of amounts, with no
       hypothesis (on a flow, read by what each part has drawn, with none on the flow). Joined to
       Flow.joint_excess_ends: the dependence that ends a part at the end of a race of joint excess
       is stated exactly, and position does not enter it; with renewal gated, the greatest parts end
       with the condition for good. Two witnesses show gated renewal and dependence each needed,
       and the clearer's web keeps the counterexample, whose loss is one of significance and needs
       a significance
Supplied premises / correspondence: none for the counting law. For the end at the race's end:
       balance at the condition across n steps of joint excess, a start below n plus the part's
       need, the part requiring the condition at that step and active only while supported. For
       the end for good: balance, only active formations giving, activity needing support, and
       renewal gated at m (Flow.joint_excess_ends' hypotheses). The continuation condition only
       as a hypothesis of Clearing.loss_needs_significance
Evidence: Becoming.RelativePosition, 40 theorems, 59 declarations, empty axiom reports; core
          receipt `20261019T110924.527968Z`; connectivity passes on the landing tree, 441 apart of 10,744 theorems, none in Becoming.RelativePosition
Boundary: that a race for position produces joint excess (a premise of the join); that any actual
          part depends on what it draws down (the dependence hypothesis, empirical for the Earth);
          positions other than the deviation from the family's total (ranks, shares); the
          dynamics by which parts race
```

The opening's sentence "We need to stop the game of winning: a zero-sum game of relative position, which, as I see it, all its winners will lose" was, by its own note, half counting and half judgment, and the v7 proposal (edit (j)) offered to mark it as a judgment. This item states the counting half on the spine and proves the second half under a stated dependence, so that the note can say exactly where it holds.

**The question.** What makes a game of relative position zero-sum, and does it say anything about whether those ahead in it continue? Where they continue or end, what decides it?

**The move.** A part's position in a finite family is its amount read against the others'. With signed amounts it is `n * a p - total ps a` (`n` the number of parts), the part's deviation from the family's mean taken `n` times. In `Nat` it is kept as two counts, the ahead count `n * a p` against the behind count `total ps a`, and a change of amounts from `a` to `b` raises `p`'s position by `riseCount ps a b p = n * b p + total ps a` against `fallCount ps a b p = n * a p + total ps b`. Nothing is assumed of the amounts: they are any reading (`pos : Nat → F → Nat`), and on a flow one reading is what each part has drawn from a condition over the steps before (`Flow.drawn`). The race is then joined to the law of joint excess (`Flow.joint_excess_ends`), with the part's position quantified over and its dependence stated exactly.

**What is proved** (`Becoming.RelativePosition`).
- **Zero-sum is counting** (`RelativePosition.positions_balance`, `change_balances`, `change_opposed`, `rest_falls_of_rises`, `not_all_rise`, `rise_needs_fall`). Over the family the ahead counts total what the behind counts total, and across every change the rise counts total what the fall counts total. So a part's change of position is the opposite of the change summed over the rest; where it rises, the rest's summed position falls; no change raises every part's position; and a part's rise needs some other part's fall. The proofs are arithmetic on totals; the dichotomy behind `rise_needs_fall` is decided by `Nat.lt_or_ge`, so the other part is found, not inferred by contradiction.
- **Whatever the amounts do** (`DrawingMore.grow_and_fall`). On a flow where two parts draw one unit each and then one and three, every part draws more across the second step, and the part that draws less falls in position while the other rises. Relative position is zero-sum even where every amount grows: a game played for it is zero-sum by this count, not by any law of what is played for.
- **On a flow, with no hypothesis** (`Flow.drawn_positions`). Read by what each part of a family has drawn from a condition, between any two steps, every law above holds, and the family has a greatest part whose position is not below the family's (`greatest_exists`, `greatest_not_behind`). "Greatest" (`Greatest`) means only that no part's amount exceeds its own.
- **The end at the race's end, exactly** (`Flow.excess_leaves_below`, `Flow.ends_at_race_end`). With balance at the condition across `n` steps of joint excess from `T`, a part that at `T + n` requires the condition, at a need greater than the level at `T` less `n`, and is active there only while supported, is not active there. No renewal need be gated for this step, and the part's position does not enter: the hypotheses are the part's dependence, its need and its activity needing support.
- **The end for good** (`Flow.race_ends_greatest`, `Flow.greatest_end_for_good`). Adding `Flow.joint_excess_ends`' hypotheses (balance, only active formations giving, activity needing support, renewal gated at `m`, a start below `n + m`): for every family and every reading of positions, the race changes positions by a zero-sum count while the level falls by at least `n`; the level stays below `m` from `T + n` on; and every part depending on the condition at a need of at least `m` is inactive from then on, the greatest parts included. In a family whose parts all so depend, at every later step there is a greatest part, and every greatest part is inactive.
- **A race that ends its greatest part** (`Race.greatest_ends`). A renewer giving two units and two parts taking two and one: while they take part each takes within what the step gives and together they take more. Read by what each has drawn, the first part is greatest at every step and rises in position across the race while the rest's summed position falls; from step two on it is inactive, as is every part, the renewer included (through `Flow.race_ends_greatest` and `Flow.joint_excess_ends`).
- **Gated renewal is needed for the end to last** (`Restored.returns`). A renewer that requires nothing gives at the race's end: the race of one step ends the part at its end (`Flow.ends_at_race_end`), and the renewal restores it from the next step on, while it is greatest at every step.
- **Dependence is needed** (`Clearing.greatest_continues`). In the clearer's web of `Becoming.Continuation`, read by what each part has drawn from the habitat, the clearer is the greatest part at every step. The habitat is drawn down jointly beyond what is given to it across two steps, from a level below two plus one, and nothing gives to it, so renewal there is gated; the dweller, which depends on the habitat, is inactive from step two on (`Flow.joint_excess_ends`). The clearer does not require the habitat, and it is active and supported at every step.
- **Its loss is one of significance, and needs a significance** (`Clearing.loss_needs_significance`). Under the continuation condition, from every standpoint, the clearer's part loses the dweller (`Clearing.free_rider_loses`); where nothing has significance it loses nothing; and either way the clearer is active and supported. The continuation condition is not the only significance that counts the loss: the clearer's own presupposition, held along sharing a condition, counts it too (`Clearing.own_presupposition`, which the v7 proposal's second review cited against "only the continuation condition makes that loss count").

**What this changes.** The zero-sum half of the opening's sentence is a theorem with no premise: whatever is played for, and whether its amounts grow or shrink, one part's rise in position is the rest's summed fall, and the race cannot raise everyone. The "winners will lose" half is a theorem under a dependence: where the race draws a shared condition down jointly beyond its renewal, that renewal depends on the condition, and those ahead depend on it at a need above what the race leaves, the race ends them with it, and being ahead changes nothing. Where those ahead do not depend on what they draw down, they can continue, and what they lose is a continuation with significance, which counts only under a significance that reaches it. Which of the two holds of the present race is not a law of the spine: it is the empirical premise the opening calls the entangled Earth. The relation to edit (ee) of the proposal: `Flow.favours_reaching_beyond` says that, where the whole gains nothing (`Flow.GainlessOn`, a premise), a rise of an observed family's stock is paid by taking from beyond it; `rise_needs_fall` is the corresponding statement for position, with no premise, since position is relative by definition.

**The sentence the opening carries.** The note [^aligned] (AI-written, so changed without a proposal; the body is untouched) carries it from this landing on, with a link to the record, in place of "That a game of relative position is zero-sum is a matter of counting, not yet stated on the formal spine. That the present race ends badly even for its winner is a judgment.":

> That a game of relative position is zero-sum is a counting law: for any amounts and any change of them, one part's rise in position is the rest's summed fall, and no change raises every part, even where every amount grows (`RelativePosition.change_balances`, `RelativePosition.not_all_rise`, `DrawingMore.grow_and_fall`). That its winners lose is proved under a stated dependence: where a race draws a shared condition down jointly beyond its renewal, the renewal depends on that condition, and those ahead depend on it at a need above what the race leaves, the race ends them with the condition, whatever their position (`Flow.race_ends_greatest`). One ahead that does not depend on what it draws down can continue (`Clearing.greatest_continues`); what it loses then is a continuation with significance, which counts under the continuation condition and under no significance at all does not (`Clearing.loss_needs_significance`). That the present race draws down conditions its leaders depend on is the empirical premise of the entangled Earth; that it ends badly even for its winner is a judgment on that premise.

**The body.** The opening's version 7 proposal, third pass, gave two body edits for this landing, (oo) and (oo′), and Ren agreed to them with the rest of version 7 ([source](../../../../sources/15-codex-theory-conversations/2026-10-19-opening-v7.md): the lander applies each item's body edit and its note together). They are applied in this landing. (oo): "a zero-sum game of relative position, which all its winners will lose wherever they live on what it draws down", in place of "which, as I see it, all its winners will lose"; this claims no more than is proved, since the loss is proved where the winners depend on what the race draws down and is not universal (`Clearing.greatest_continues`), and the factual premise that today's winners do so live is the entangled Earth, stated in the body as such. (oo′): "A race of position cannot raise everyone, and where the whole gains nothing, every reward for a rise is paid by taking from what those rewarded do not couple into", in the incentives paragraph; the first clause is `not_all_rise`, with no premise, and the note [^race] now cites it beside `Flow.favours_reaching_beyond`. No formal join between `rise_needs_fall` and `favours_reaching_beyond` was made.

*Reading* [AI reading, open]. Relative position is a reading that sums to nothing by its construction; the race for it is a relation among the parts, not a quantity they produce. What the race spends is real (here the level of a shared condition), and what decides whether those ahead go on is their dependence, not their place. So the race's verdict on its leaders is the dependence's, read off the relations they continue through, as the one-unfolding method asks. Whether that supports or damages 生生 is not decided here.

**Not done.** Positions read as ranks (the ranks of a family sum to a fixed count) or as shares; a race dynamic in which parts behind raise their take, and whether it produces joint excess; several shared conditions with different needs; the empirical premise for any actual race; an independent review.

**Self-review.** The statements were read against the Lean.
- `riseCount`/`fallCount` are the two counts of `n * (b p - a p) - (total b - total a)`: `p` rises exactly where `fallCount < riseCount`; no subtraction is used, so the laws hold in `Nat` without truncation.
- `change_opposed` states the family as `pre ++ p :: post`, so the part may sit anywhere in it; `total_split` moves it to the front with `total_append` and `Nat.add_left_comm`.
- `rise_needs_fall` finds the falling part by the decided dichotomy `below_somewhere_or_not` (`Nat.lt_or_ge`); in the other branch the totals would be strictly ordered, contradicting `change_balances`.
- `Flow.race_ends_greatest` quantifies over the family, membership and greatestness and uses neither: it is `Flow.joint_excess_ends` with the positions read alongside, which is the claim (position does not protect). `Flow.ends_at_race_end` needs no gating, and its need hypothesis is the part's own need at the race's end.
- `Restored.returns` derives the part's inactivity at step one through `Flow.ends_at_race_end`, not from the stipulated activity; the renewer gives at step one and does not require the condition, so gating fails there exactly.
- `Clearing.greatest_continues` derives the dweller's end through `Flow.joint_excess_ends` on the habitat with gating vacuous (`Clearing.habitat_ungiven`), and adds `Clearing.acting`, which the earlier witness did not state.
- The module imports only `Becoming.Significance`; every declaration has an empty axiom report (scratch build and core receipt).

## 201. Which physical premises give the least loss (T1)

```text
Result(s): least-loss-from-entropy-production (new); reused: entropy-history-and-record,
           rest-at-every-resolution, continued-change-needs-openness, rest-with-refinement-counted,
           premises-read-off-the-exchange
Delta: the physical premises under which the spine's dissipation, its first law and its
       unit-free form hold, each step from the premises to the spine proved on the spine's own
       flows: the second law read in available work is the first law at the unit; strict
       irreversibility of every taking exchange with whole units, or a floor of destruction at
       least the unit (Landauer), is dissipation; a floor survives refinement; bounded efficiency
       is loss in proportion; the statistical second law keeps rest almost surely
Supplied premises / correspondence: that amounts are available work, the exergy balance, the
       second law per exchange, irreversibility or a floor, whole units, the integral fluctuation
       theorem; each is a hypothesis of a theorem and a correspondence to physics, not proved
Evidence: periphery module EntropyProduction (24 theorems, 33 declarations; Lean 4.30.0-rc2 and the
          pinned Mathlib; axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound only), periphery receipt
          `20261019T082858.129214Z`, checker check_entropy_production.py; the core modules it
          imports match passed receipts
Boundary: the step from physics to the Lean; Landauer's bound itself; real systems' fit; a core
          (prelude-only) form; finite-time floors; the rest family in expectation at a refining unit
```

The opening says the conditional laws hold "wherever, as in ours, nothing comes from nothing and nothing passes on without loss". The v7 proposal's edit (d) drops "as in ours" for three reasons: the spine's least loss of one whole unit per uptake is stronger than the statistical second law (chapter §8.7); `Passing` is a finite, enclosed, lossless world that never rests (`Passing.passes`); and at a refining unit rest fails unless the refinement is counted (`Becoming.Resolution`, `Feeding.endless`). Balance needs no bridge (it holds by reading, premise card C), so only the loss half needs physics behind it.

**The question.** Does `Flow.Dissipative` (on every family without repetition closed across a step, each formation taking part gives back at least one unit less than it takes, `World.Dissipative` being the world's flow so), or its unit-free form `Flow.DissipativeBy q`, follow from accepted physics, and for which class of systems? Where it does not, what weaker premise does physics give and which rest law survives under it?

**The move.** Read the amounts. Energy is the wrong reading: it is conserved, and with the environment counted as a condition every exchange is lossless, while with the environment left out heat drawn from it gives a formation more than it took. Available work (exergy, relative to one environment at temperature T₀) is the reading under which both halves of the opening's sentence are physics. Each unit of amount is `u` of available work; `σ t f` is the exergy formation `f`'s exchange destroys across the step from `t`. Conditions hold every amount and formations hold none: a store inside a process is counted as a condition, so exergy a formation takes and does not give back is destroyed, not kept. The physics then enters as hypotheses on the spine's flows in a periphery module, `EntropyProduction`, which imports the core and Mathlib's reals and measures; the core does not import it.

**What is proved** (each a theorem of `EntropyProduction`, from the stated hypotheses):

- **The exergy balance and the record.** `ExergyBalance L u σ`: over every closed family without repetition, `u · given + σ = u · taken` for each formation taking part. This is the Gouy–Stodola balance, exact bookkeeping of energy and entropy together. `SecondLaw L σ`: `0 ≤ σ`, no exchange destroys negative exergy. Under both, the destroyed exergy is the residue counted in units (`ExergyBalance.destroyed_eq_residue`): the record of `Flow.dissipatesOn_iff_conserved` is the destroyed exergy, and Kelvin–Planck (no process draws work from the environment's heat at one temperature) is the record being taken from by none. So the core's decomposition (least loss = first law + a record of at least one unit in the conserved amount) reads: the exergy balance is the conserved amount with its record, and the strict part is that each taking exchange destroys at least one unit.
- **The second law is the spine's first law.** `gainless_of_secondLaw`: the exergy balance and the second law give `Flow.Gainless` at the unit. They do not give dissipation: `Passing` meets both with nothing destroyed and is not dissipative (`secondLaw_not_dissipative`, `passing_balance`). Physically that is an isolated reversible exchange, a unit carried back and forth as between two coupled oscillators; Liouville's theorem allows it, and the spine's revisiting of a finite lossless enclosure (`Flow.Balances.recurs`) is the Poincaré recurrence of such systems.
- **Strict irreversibility with whole units.** `dissipative_of_irreversible`: where, in addition, every exchange that takes from a closed family destroys some exergy (`Irreversible`), the flow is dissipative. The step is integrality: with whole units of amount, giving back strictly less is giving back at least one unit less. Physics gives the strictness for every exchange run at a finite pace in contact with its surroundings (only quasi-static processes destroy nothing). Whole units are carriers of one free energy each (ATP in a cell, at about 20 kT per hydrolysis; photons of one frequency; bits of one memory); where carriers of several kinds are counted together, their free energies must be whole multiples of one unit.
- **A floor in energy, and refinement.** `loss_of_floor`, `dissipative_of_floor`, `loss_at_finer_unit`: where every exchange that takes destroys at least `s` (`DestroysAtLeast`), the loss counted at the unit `u` is at least every whole `n` with `n · u ≤ s`, the flow is dissipative at every unit `u ≤ s`, and at an `r`-fold finer unit the loss is at least `r` units. Landauer's bound gives such a floor: erasing a bit at temperature T destroys at least kT ln 2 in expectation (Landauer 1961; Bennett 1982; confirmed by Bérut et al. 2012 and by Jun, Gavrilov and Bechhoefer 2014; its general derivation has been disputed, Norton 2005 and 2011). So the class is: exchanges at a temperature T > 0 each of which, when it takes, merges at least one bit of the state it acts on. The floor is an amount of energy, not one unit of whatever resolution, so this class is the one where the least loss survives the refinement that breaks it in `Becoming.Resolution`; strictness without a floor does not (a strict loss can fall below every unit).
- **Bounded efficiency, unit-free.** `dissipativeBy_of_efficiency`: where every exchange over a closed family destroys at least a `(q + 1)`th of the exergy it takes (a second-law efficiency of at most `q/(q + 1)`), the flow is dissipative in proportion `q`, whatever the unit. This is the premise of the amount law at every resolution (`Flow.uptake_bound`, rest-at-every-resolution).
- **The statistical form.** Over runs drawn from a measure (`ExpectedDissipatesOn`: in expectation the family's replenishment and its takers are within its uptake), dissipation in expectation follows from dissipation on every run (`ExpectedDissipatesOn.of_pathwise`), and from an exergy balance on each run whose destruction `D` may be negative on a single run, with expected destruction at least `u` for each formation that takes (`ExpectedDissipatesOn.of_exergy`; Landauer in expectation is this premise). Balanced on each run and dissipated on in expectation from step `T`: the expected stock falls across each step by at least the expected takers (`expected_runs_down`); the expected takers over every stretch are within the expected stock at `T` (`expected_takers_within`); the probabilities of taking, summed over every stretch, are within it (`taking_probability_within`); and, by Borel–Cantelli, on almost every run, from some step on, no formation takes (`taking_not_recurring_ae`). The core's law is stated as non-recurrence, constructively; this one names a step on almost every run, classically. What does not survive is the pathwise bound: in `Fluctuation` both runs are balanced and closed, the family is dissipated on in expectation at every step, and one run gains, so its flow is neither gainless nor dissipative (`Fluctuation.gains_in_one_run`).
- **The second law in expectation from the fluctuation theorem.** Where the entropy production `S` (in units of k) meets the integral fluctuation theorem `E[exp(−S)] = 1` (Jarzynski 1997, Crooks 1999, Seifert 2005), its expectation is not negative (`expected_production_nonneg`), and a run producing at most `−a` has probability at most `exp(−a)` (`gain_probability_le`). Gains on single small runs are observed (Wang et al. 2002; Collin et al. 2005). So the second law physics gives at small scales is the expectation form, and the expectation form is enough for rest almost surely.

**Which physical premise gives which spine premise.**

| Physical premise (correspondence) | Spine premise (theorem) |
|---|---|
| Amounts as available work; Gouy–Stodola exergy balance; second law per exchange | `Flow.Gainless` (`gainless_of_secondLaw`); the destroyed exergy is the record of `dissipatesOn_iff_conserved` |
| + every taking exchange irreversible (finite pace, in contact) + whole units of one free energy | `Flow.Dissipative` (`dissipative_of_irreversible`) |
| + Landauer: each taking exchange merges at least one bit at T > 0; unit at most kT ln 2 | `Flow.Dissipative` at every such unit, `r` units at an `r`-fold finer one (`dissipative_of_floor`, `loss_at_finer_unit`) |
| Second-law efficiency at most `q/(q + 1)` per exchange | `Flow.DissipativeBy q` (`dissipativeBy_of_efficiency`) |
| Second law and Landauer only in expectation (fluctuation theorems) | `ExpectedDissipatesOn`; taking does not recur almost surely (`taking_not_recurring_ae`) |
| Isolated reversible dynamics | none: `Passing` meets the second law and is not dissipative |

**What the opening could then carry.** Not "as in ours" bare: physics does not make every exchange of our world lose, since isolated reversible exchange exists and single small runs gain. The strongest exact sentence these results support, in place of "as in ours", is:

> The rest holds wherever nothing comes from nothing and nothing passes on without loss: in our world, wherever each exchange that takes forgets something of what it held, since there the second law and Landauer's bound make it lose available work; and where the loss holds only on average, as at the smallest scales, taking from what is closed still ends on almost every course.

A shorter form: "…wherever nothing comes from nothing and nothing passes on without loss, as in ours wherever exchanges forget." The last clause states only what is proved in expectation (`taking_not_recurring_ae`); the world's rest theorems are not restated in expectation here. Its footnote would cite this record and say that the step from physics to the spine is a stated correspondence, the class being exchanges at a temperature above zero that each merge at least a bit of the state they act on. The body is in Ren's voice; the sentence is handed to the opening proposal (board item R20) as a proposal, not applied.

**Counter-review (the author's).** (1) *Is the exergy balance smuggling the conclusion?* No: it is bookkeeping (a definition of `σ`), and the second law alone gives only `Gainless`; `Passing` shows that the strict part is a further premise. (2) *Does Landauer apply to "taking"?* Only where the taking exchange is logically irreversible on what it acts on; a logically reversible exchange (Bennett) can in principle destroy arbitrarily little, and that is outside the class. (3) *Whole units are artificial.* They are the integrality route only; the floor route needs no integrality of the physics, only that the unit be within the floor, and the proportion route needs neither. (4) *The almost-sure law is classical.* Yes, it lives in the periphery with Mathlib's axioms reported; the core's constructive non-recurrence is not replaced. (5) *Per-step floors at finite time* (thermodynamic length, Salamon and Berry 1983, Sivak and Crooks 2012; the thermodynamic uncertainty relation, Barato and Seifert 2015) are further sources of `DestroysAtLeast` and are not stated here.

**What would change it.** A physical system whose taking exchanges merge states at a temperature above zero and destroy less than kT ln 2 on average would refute the correspondence (and Landauer's bound); a core form with rational amounts would move the deterministic laws into the core.

The relations of the places in the Changes (Y2, [section 195](#195-the-relations-of-the-places-in-the-changes-y2)) left as not done 王弼's reading that the bottom and top places have no place, and the reading of one line answered by all the others; the 《周易略例》 was not preserved here. This continues the request of 19 October 2026, “我要你把这个系统完全建立起来，要变成库的一部分，要确保它在spine上有明确的mapping” ([words](../../../../sources/15-codex-theory-conversations/2026-10-19-the-changes-on-the-spine.md)); the request is provenance, and the argument is below.

**The question.** Y2 stated 正 at all six places by parity. Its census of the 小象 found one exception of place, 需上六's 「雖不當位」, and three passages (小畜 and 大有 上下應之, 夬 乘五剛) read one line against all the others, wider than its relations of heights and seams. 王弼 reads the exception as evidence that the bottom and top places have no fixed place, and a line alone of its kind as the 主 of its hexagram. Do these readings hold as relations on the spine, how do they meet Y2's, and which reading does the text use when it speaks of place?

**The move.** Both are relations read at other sites than Y2's. The second relation reads the phase only at the four places between the ends (`fixedPhase : Place → Option Bool`, `none` at the ends), so a line at an end neither holds nor fails a place; it stands beside `inPhase`, not in place of it. The answer of two lines is read at any pair of places (`answers`), and a sole line is one that answers every other. Every proof is by exhaustive cases on six Booleans or by rewriting with the laws of `Becoming.HexagramPlaces`; no `propext` enters.

**What is proved** (`Becoming.HexagramSites`).
- **王弼's dilemma.** Of two lines that differ at a place, every parity of the place puts one of them in phase (`one_in_phase_of_parity`). 需's top line is broken and 乾's unbroken, and the 小象 and the 文言 say neither has a place (「雖不當位」, 「貴而无位」), so no parity of the top place makes both statements true (`top_no_parity`). The text fixes the other parities: any parity on which the 小象's statements of place hold gives places 3, 4 and 5 the parity of `odd`, and one on which the statements of 中正 hold gives place 2 (`statements_fix_parity`, `centre_fixes_parity`); no statement of place in the 小象 is at the bottom (`placeStatements_between`).
- **Under the second relation.** With 乾's and 需's top lines, all 28 statements of place of the 小象 and the 文言 hold (`placeStatements_hold`, `xu_top_no_place`, `qian_top`). The 彖's 9 statements of the place of one line hold (`tuanPlaceStatements_agree`); its 5 statements of the place of the whole hold between the ends, and only 2 at six places (`tuanWhole_between`, `tuanWhole_six`): 蹇 and 漸 have their bottom line out of phase, 漸 its top too, and 歸妹 both ends in phase. Every line between the ends is in phase exactly at 既濟, 蹇, 漸 and 家人, and none exactly at 未濟, 歸妹, 解 and 睽 (`allHold_iff`, `noneHold_iff`); read at its four places the second relation glues there and nowhere else, so no frame of context-free claims fits it under any process (`between_glues_iff`, `between_no_free_frame`).
- **What it tells.** Configurations alike between the ends have the same lines there, so the inner seams and the middle opposition are told (`sameBetween_phase`, `inner_seams_told`, `opposed_mid_told`); changing an end line keeps every phase between the ends and turns the opposition and the alternation beside it (`ends_not_told`). Under waxing and waning the line entering place 2 takes the phase opposite to its phase at the bottom (`fixedPhase_waxWane_enters`), a line rising from 2 to 5 holds its place at exactly two of them (`course_between`), and the phases between the ends are not a lumping the law goes alike across (`betweenPhases_not_goAlike`).
- **The sole line.** Two lines answer where they differ (`answers`), at any pair; opposition and alternation are this relation at their pairs (`opposed_answers`, `alternates_answers`). A line answering every other is in a configuration with one unbroken or one broken line (`sole_count`, `soleAny_count`), and it is unique (`sole_unique`); the twelve configurations are the uniform ones with one line changed (`sole_iff_flip`). Of the twelve, four hold their place between the ends, four are out of phase there and four are at the ends (`sole_places`). The configuration is opposed at the sole line's height only (`sole_opposition`), while 節, opposed at one height, has no sole line (`jie_one_opposed`); below a sole broken line is the only fall and above it the only rise (`sole_broken_seams`), and a sole broken top line is exactly 夬 (`guai_iff`).
- **Under the laws of change.** No configuration with a sole line has one a step of waxing and waning later (`soleAny_waxWane`); six steps on the sole line is back at its place (`sole_six`); a sole line at the top passes out, leaving a uniform configuration, and two steps on a sole line stands at the bottom (`sole_top_passes`). Changing a sole line gives a uniform configuration, and changing a line of a uniform one gives a sole line (`changes_run_sole`).
- **Along the unfolding.** Every law is read along runs: of waxing and waning (`run_between_rises`, `run_placedCount`, `run_course_between`, `run_between_six`, `run_sole`), of the law backward (`backward_between`, `backward_sole`), of the change of one line (`changes_run_between`, `changes_run_ends`, `changes_run_sole`) and of any process (`between_shown_along_runs`, `between_glue_along_run`, `sole_shown_along_run`, `answers_shown_along_run`).

**The text, the passages and the censuses.** The 《周易略例》 was retrieved through the MediaWiki API (the index and seven pages, revision ids, timestamps and SHA-256 in [PROVENANCE.json](../../../../sources/zhouyi-yizhuan/PROVENANCE.json)); only 明彖 marks 王弼's text, and every quotation is from a paragraph of his, not from 邢璹's notes. 23 passages cite the module (14 agreements, 5 exact scopes, 4 divergences); the map now holds 88 (50, 26, 12). Five passages of Y2 change: 小畜's 上下應之 and 夬's 乘五剛 from scope to agreement, 需上六 from divergence to agreement under the second relation, 大有 a divergence still for 尊位 with its 上下應之 now in the module, and the reading of the 小象's census of place. [verify_mapping.py](development/y1-changes/verify_mapping.py) now also checks the 小象's statements of place under the second relation with 乾上九 (no exception) and eight more censuses: the 彖's statements of the place of one line (9) and of the whole (5) and its 上下應 (3); the line texts' 中 (11, all between the ends, 5 middle; of the 5 of 中行, 2 middle) and 位 (1, 萃九五, in place); the 大象's 中 (8, each the lower trigram's image within the upper's) and 位 (2, 鼎 and 艮, of the 君子); and the 小象's 中 (51, 47 middle; 泰六四 中心, 復六四 中行, 震上六 中未得 and 豐九四 日中 are not the middle places). The lists of the 彖 and the line texts are compared with the Lean's; the others with the exceptions the script records.

**The integration.** 23 of the module's 103 theorems stand apart from the base: 21 roots, what the 彖, the 小象, the 文言, the line texts and 王弼's 略例下 say of named configurations, the censuses, 王弼's dilemma as a fact about two configurations, and the witnesses and census of the twelve configurations with a sole line, registered as model witnesses, and 2 lemmas only they use. Every law of the two relations is read on the base along runs. On this tree there are 59 dependency components, 20 spine theorems outside the main one, and 161 statements on both families.

**What this changes.** 王弼's reading is a second relation, not a correction of the first. `inPhase` is the parity of six places and stays as Y2 stated it; `holdsPlace` is the relation the 彖 and the 象 use when they speak of place: under it every statement of place they make holds, 需上六 and the five statements of the whole among them, of which the parity of six places makes only two true. His argument is a law of the text's statements: no parity of the top place fits 乾上九 and 需上六 together. The ends are not outside the relations: they are where a line enters and leaves, and the phase a line takes at place 2 is set by what it was at the bottom, so the second relation cannot be followed without the ends, which is the structural content of 「初上者，始終之象也」. The line answered by all others is one relation, the answer at every pair, read from one line; it is unique, independent of place and phase, and it never lasts a step of waxing and waning: it enters at the bottom, rises, passes out at the top, and the uniform configuration it leaves is where the next one enters. 王弼's 主 is taken as this relation; his 治眾 is not, since the relation is symmetric. The 大象's 中 is the relation of the two trigrams, and the line texts' 中 is mostly the middle of something, not the middle places.

*Reading* [AI reading, D53]. 王弼 read the text against itself and found the relation it uses; on the spine his argument is a finite law of what the text says, and the relation he named is the one under which the text speaks consistently of place. His ruler is a relation of one line to all, symmetric, which the law of waxing and waning carries through every place and out; what he adds, rule, rank and beauty, is what the theory does not derive from the structure.

**Not done.** 王弼's 周易注, line by line; the other rulers he names (the middle line, a line in place, a line answered at its height) as relations of their own; 時 read with 位 (明卦適變通爻); the 文言's statements of place; 邢璹's notes separated from 王弼's text outside 明彖; an independent review.

**Self-review.** The statements were read against the Lean, and the docstrings say what it proves (`sole_top_passes` gives the sole line at the bottom two steps on, not one; `course_between` counts the places held by one line as it rises, not by a configuration). Each passage was read in its page of the preserved revision, each census against the pages by script, and each reading against what its declarations state; 「為為兌之主」 and 「雲」 are the edition's and are kept.

## 203. Place/transition nets on the spine (PT1)

```text
Result(s): place-transition-nets-on-the-spine (new); reused: counterfactual-is-the-course,
           rising-and-falling-in-one-exchange, no-finite-part-bears-taking,
           continued-change-needs-openness, own-count-misses-joint-excess; related:
           premises-read-off-the-exchange
Delta: the first instance theorem for a formalism defined outside the theory. Place/transition nets
       (pre and post multiplicities, markings, steps with repetition, enabling, firing, firing
       sequences), stated by their own rules with no word of the spine, are a law of exchange whose
       course is the net's flow and whose levels are its markings; each premise the spine's laws use
       is derived from the net's definitions or characterised exactly by a named property of the net;
       the laws are restated for nets; where a premise fails, a net where the law fails
Supplied premises / correspondence: none in the Lean beyond the net's named properties (finitely many
       places listed once, with equality decided; fired transitions that lose weighted tokens, or a
       strict P-subinvariant; a gated place; finitely many transitions for the world form); that a
       chemical, biological or computing system is a given net is a modelling correspondence
Evidence: Becoming.PlaceTransitionNets, 73 theorems, 106 declarations, empty axiom reports; core
          receipt `20261019T122417.550535Z`; connectivity check passes, 464 apart of 10,920, 0 in the module
Boundary: inhibitor arcs, capacities, timed and stochastic nets (rates), continuous nets; nets with
          infinitely many places; the world form's reading of transitions as standing at one
Output -> input: an outside formalism meeting the spine's premises by its own definitions, for the
          opening's notes (R20), for E1's premises read off a law of exchange, and as the template for
          further instance theorems (stochastic reaction networks pathwise, Markov kernels on counts)
```

The second review of the opening proposal ([drafts/2026-10-10-opening/history/OPENING-V7-PROPOSAL.md](../../../../drafts/2026-10-10-opening/history/OPENING-V7-PROPOSAL.md), "New work that would allow stronger claims", item 2) ranked as the direct answer to an outside critique, that the theory proves the rules of its own invented universe and then assumes that ours runs the same way, an instance theorem for a formalism defined outside the theory, with each premise derived or characterised exactly. None existed.

**The choice.** Two candidates were named: discrete Petri nets, or chemical reaction networks with whole-number counts, and finite Markov kernels on counts. Place/transition nets are taken. Their commitments are the spine's own: discrete steps, whole-number amounts, and change as what is taken and given; so the map is the identity on what each says, and nothing is approximated. They are a standard formalism of concurrency, chemistry and biology, defined long before this repository, with known laws (P-invariants, siphons, termination by a linear ranking) against which the instance can be checked. A Markov kernel assigns probabilities, which are not whole-number amounts; an instance would need a second correspondence, a law over distributions or over sample paths. Its pathwise half is already this one: every sample path of a stochastic reaction network's jump chain fires one enabled reaction at a time, so it is a sequential firing sequence of the underlying net, and the laws below hold on every path (a modelling remark, not in the Lean).

**The net, by its own rules.** `Net T P` holds `pre f p` and `post f p`. A step is a list of transitions, repetition allowed (a multiset: step semantics); it is enabled at a marking where it consumes from each place at most what the place holds; firing removes what it consumes and adds what it produces; a schedule is a firing sequence from `M₀` where each step is enabled at the marking reached. A net is pure where no transition consumes from and produces into one place; a schedule is sequential where at most one transition fires at a time. None of these definitions uses the spine. Weights `y` on the places read tokens in units, as a P-semiflow does.

**The map.** In units `y`, the net's exchange law takes `y p * pre f p` and gives `y p * post f p` whatever has stood (`Net.law`); the flow along a schedule has the schedule's steps as the formations taking part (`Net.flow`); the web reads the markings in units, a transition active exactly where it fires, requiring and drawing on the places it consumes from at its weighted multiplicity (`Net.web`). Read as one world (`Net.world`), places and transitions are the relata: a transition stands at one, the structure of the net, and a place at its weighted marking, active while marked.

**What holds by the net's definitions.**
- The law reads what has stood (`Net.law_nonanticipating`, by `rfl`: it reads nothing), and the course it generates along a schedule is the net's flow (`Net.course_eq`, by `rfl`). Along a firing sequence its levels are the markings in units (`Net.Fires.levels_eq`).
- **Balance is the firing rule.** Along a firing sequence the flow balances the markings in any units (`Net.Fires.balances`), and with every weight positive it balances exactly where the schedule is a firing sequence (`Net.balances_iff`): a step not enabled breaks balance at the place it overdraws, because the marking floors at zero.
- **Feasibility.** Enabling gives the law's feasibility (`Net.Fires.feasible`), so `ExchangeLaw.course_balances_iff` applies (`Net.Fires.course_balances`). Feasibility is weaker: it lets a step use what it produces in the same step. It is enabling exactly for pure nets fired one transition at a time (`Net.fires_iff_feasible`), and both conditions are needed: a catalyst, one transition consuming and producing a token at an empty place, is feasible and does not fire (`Net.catalyst_feasible_not_fires`), and so is a concurrent step of a pure net in which a sink uses what a source produces (`Net.relay_feasible_not_fires`). The spine's feasibility is the firing rule with token reuse within a step.
- **The tying premises.** Only active transitions give (`Net.acting`), only active transitions take and only from what they draw on (`Net.taking`), and along a firing sequence activity needs support (`Net.Fires.dependent`): enabling a step bounds each transition's multiplicity at each place by the marking.

**What holds exactly under a named property of the net.**
- **Dissipation is a strict P-subinvariant.** A transition loses in units `y` over the places where it produces no more weighted tokens than it consumes, and fewer when it consumes any (`Net.Loses`; implied by `y·post < y·pre`, a strict P-subinvariant, `Net.Loses.of_lt`). For finitely many places listed once, with equality of places decided, the flow is dissipative exactly where every transition it fires loses (`Net.dissipative_iff`): over any family closed across a step the totals are those over all places (`Net.total_eq_closed`). The sign form admits null transitions, consuming and producing nothing weighted; a strict P-subinvariant excludes transitions with no weighted input.
- **Enclosure** holds at every step of a net with finitely many places (`Net.enclosed`, and `Net.world_enclosed` for the world).
- **Census and embodiment** hold of the world with finitely many transitions (`Net.world_counted`, `Net.world_embodied`), and the world balances and dissipates where the flow does (`Net.Fires.world_balanced`, `Net.world_dissipative`).

**The laws, for nets.** Along a firing sequence of a net with finitely many places whose fired transitions lose:
- a step raising one place's weighted marking lowers another's (`Net.rise_with_fall`, from `Flow.rise_with_fall`; in tokens, `Net.rise_with_fall_tokens`);
- the transitions consuming anything, fired over the first `n` steps, number at most the initial weighted token count (`Net.takers_within`, from `Flow.Balances.takers_within`), the classical bound of a firing sequence by a decreasing linear ranking `y·M`; so firing them does not recur (`Net.taking_not_recurring`);
- that the marking stops changing from some step on cannot be refuted (`Net.change_stops_unrefuted`, from `Flow.change_stops_unrefuted_around`; in tokens with positive weights, `Net.marking_stops_unrefuted`), and, with finitely many transitions, every premise of `World.rests_unrefuted_enclosed` holds of the world, so that from some step on no place is emptied or newly marked cannot be refuted (`Net.rests_unrefuted`). Naming the step is a principle of omniscience, as on the spine: the schedule is any function.
- **The siphon law is the joint-excess law.** A place is gated at `m` where every transition producing into it consumes at least `m` tokens from it. Where a place is gated at `m`, `n` steps of a firing sequence each consuming from it more than they produce, starting below `n + m`, leave every transition consuming at least `m` from it dead from then on (`Net.gated_ends`, from `Flow.joint_excess_ends`). With `m = 1` and `n = 0`, an empty place every producer of which consumes it stays empty and every transition consuming it is dead (`Net.siphon_empty`): the one-place case of the classical law that an emptied siphon stays empty, which in reaction networks is the extinction of an autocatalytic species (`A + X → 2X`).

**Where a premise fails, the law fails.** The conservative cycle (`Net.cycle`), one token moved back and forth between two places, fires forever; its world balances, has a census, is embodied and enclosed at every step (`Net.cycle_premises`), and is not dissipative (`Net.cycle_not_dissipative`); its marking changes at every step (`Net.cycle_changes`, the negation of the flow form's conclusion) and its world never rests (`Net.cycle_never_rests`). The fed place (`Net.fed`): a place emptied by its consumer is refilled by a transition that does not consume it; its flow balances, one step of joint excess starts below `1 + 1`, the place is not gated, and the consumer is active two steps later, so the conclusion of `Flow.joint_excess_ends` fails (`Net.fed_refills`).

**The integration.** The first connectivity check found 3 of the module's 73 theorems standing apart from the base: the fed place's firing and its refilling, stated of the net alone, and the relay's purity. The fed place's failure was then stated on the flow and the web, as the failure of `Flow.joint_excess_ends`'s conclusion with its other hypotheses holding, and the purity joined to the relay's feasible course; now 0 of 73 stand apart. On this tree there are 59 dependency components, 20 spine theorems outside the main one, and 161 statements on both families.

**What this changes.** For one standard formalism defined outside the theory, the spine's premises are not stipulations about an invented universe: balance and the tying premises are the net's firing rule, read; dissipation is a named, checkable property of a net (a strict P-subinvariant on what fires); enclosure is its finiteness. The laws of rising with falling, of bounded taking, of rest and of joint excess are then theorems about every net with that property, and they coincide with laws Petri-net theory already knows (termination by a decreasing linear ranking, the siphon property), which is a check that the instance reads the nets correctly. Where the property fails, as in a conservative cycle, the law fails, so the premise is doing work. What remains a correspondence is the step from a physical system to a net: which places, transitions and weights it has.

*Reading* [AI reading]. The opening's `[^proof]` note carries, citing the record: "The laws hold, as theorems, of every Petri net with finitely many places, along every firing sequence: its flow balances its markings exactly because the firing rule is respected; and where each transition it fires consumes more weighted tokens than it produces (a strict P-subinvariant), a place gains tokens only as another loses them, the firings that consume number at most the tokens at the start, and that its marking comes to rest cannot be refuted, while an emptied place that only its own consumers replenish stays empty. The conservative cycle, which loses nothing, never rests." Its body takes the third-pass edit (pp), agreed with the v7 opening ([proposal, third pass](../../../../drafts/2026-10-10-opening/history/OPENING-V7-PROPOSAL.md#third-pass-edits-for-results-verified-and-queued-19-october)): after "can check for itself", "Nor are these laws of a world made for them alone: they hold, as theorems, of systems defined without them, every place/transition net among them, each premise following from the net's own firing rule or stated as a property of the net that anyone can check." The world form's reading of a transition as standing at one is the AI's; the flow form needs no such reading.

**Not done.** Inhibitor arcs, capacities, and timed, stochastic and continuous nets; the stochastic laws (expected counts, fluctuations), which T1 studies for dissipation; siphons of more than one place; nets with infinitely many places, where enclosure is a property of the step and not of the net; deciding reachability or coverability; an independent review.

**Self-review.** The statements were read against the Lean: every theorem named above is in the module with the hypotheses given here, the counterexamples are computed by `rfl` and kernel reduction, and no match with overlapping patterns or library lemma bringing `propext` is used (the cycle's and the world's exchange are written as nested exhaustive matches for that reason).

## 204. The least loss as a premise of rest (LL1)

```text
Result(s): least-loss-rest (new)
Delta: the rest family's dependence on whole-number amounts, stated in prose by R20 (chapter item 4,
       §1 "Limits of the rest theorem"), is now a premise of a theorem. The descent every rest law
       uses is stated over amounts that may be dense (Amounts: an order that addition keeps and
       cancels, nothing least), with two premises named: a least loss ε at each change counted, and
       the stock lying within finitely many copies of ε. Whole numbers are the instance (ε one, every
       stock within its own count of ones plus one): the spine's two descents, its family laws, that
       standing stops changing, and the rest theorem World.rests_unrefuted_enclosed are proved again
       from the law, statements unchanged. Each premise is needed: Halving (dyadic, dense and Archimedean, no least
       loss) and Layered (a least loss, a stock beyond every multiple of it) never rest. Approach to rest needs no
       least loss: in Archimedean amounts, for every ε above nothing, fewer than some count of steps lose at least
       ε (a bound on the count, no decision); Halving approaches rest without reaching it. Over finitely many
       configurations a loss above nothing needs a law that merges (joined to Becoming.Recurrence)
Supplied premises / correspondence: the least loss ε and the bound of the stock by copies of ε are

       of the approach law (Amounts.few_large_losses_of_archimedean, Amounts.approaches_rest)
```
