```text
       with transmission raises the share ratio at least as (a/b)^n; a draw that exceeds
       everything drawn before leaves more than half the stock at every step it is met
Supplied premises / correspondence: none for the readings and their order. Couplings holding at
       every step, bounded starting gaps and bounded strengths for the pace laws; transmission
       (carriers' offspring carry, others' next generation is among their offspring) for the
       selection; balance and nothing given for the draw. The continuation condition appears only
       as the conclusion Unrestricted of the three bounded readings
Evidence: Becoming.MutualDependence, 33 theorems, 42 declarations, empty axiom reports; core
          receipt `20261019T144846.235357Z`; connectivity passes on the landing tree, 495 apart of 11,486 theorems, 3 of the 33 in Becoming.MutualDependence: the pace of a selection, stated for any listing of offspring (`carriers_grow`, `others_bounded` and their root `share_ratio_pow`, registered as general structure: the base reads one step of it through support, where the unsupported others leave none)
Boundary: that a dependence acts as a coupling by level with positive strength at every step (the
          meeting of the formation-level and condition-level statements); that amounts, not
          differences, grow so under the first law; the transmission premise; whether any actual
          web is mutually dependent and how fast its couplings act
```

**The question.** The opening says that the Earth "has become a highly entangled system", that every country and person "is heavily coupled into it", and that the logic of winning is being trained into the next intelligence "at an exponential pace, which leaves us very little time to react". The note on those sentences had read "entangled" as couplings on loops and shown only that loops are needed for growth beyond every polynomial, not that they are enough. Ren's reply of 19 October ([words](../../../../sources/15-codex-theory-conversations/2026-10-19-entangled-mutual-dependence.md)) agreed that "entangled" should read as mutual dependence or shared conditions, and asked to close the gap. What does mutual dependence state about formations, and what does it give for pace?

**The readings.** `Becoming.Feedback` already has four closures of a formation. Three of them, read as the whole, give three readings of an entangled web. Sharing conditions throughout: every system the whole. Mutual dependence: every influence closure the whole, so every continuation can be affected, at some remove, by every other. Mutual feeding: every feeding closure the whole, so every continuation is fed, at some remove, by every other. The order is strict. In the clearer's web every system is the whole, yet the dweller lies beyond the clearer's influence closure, since the dweller exchanges with nothing (`Clearing.shares_not_mutual`). In `Drawing`, a balanced pair each taking from what the other requires with nothing given, each can affect the other while neither feeds the other (`Drawing.mutual_not_fed`). `Overshoot`, where each feeds the other's condition, is mutually fed (`Overshoot.mutuallyFed`). Mutual dependence is the reading that fits "entangled". Sharing a condition does not entangle two formations that never affect each other (`Static.shares_unaffected` is the bare case), and mutual feeding asks that the entanglement be one of support, while `Drawing` is a race. Influence and reach are converse (`Flow.withinInfluence_iff_withinReach`, an instance of `WithinClosure.converse` of `Becoming.Response`). So a flow is mutually dependent exactly where every reach closure is the whole (`Flow.mutuallyDependent_iff_reach`): whatever a formation affects can affect it back, and every link of affecting lies on a loop through the whole. That was the content of the loop reading, now stated between formations.

**Where it meets significance.** Under each reading, significance bounded by the matching closure, the system, the influence closure or the feeding closure of each center, is the continuation condition (`Flow.SharesThroughout.unrestricted`, `Flow.MutuallyDependent.unrestricted`, `Flow.MutuallyFed.unrestricted`). The last extends `Flow.feeding_unrestricted_of_common`, which needed one condition that every formation requires and gives to at one step, to any web of mutual feeding. The opening's sentence "whoever counts all that feeds its own continuation already counts what the one step counts" therefore holds wherever continuations feed one another at some remove, not only around one shared condition. That the actual Earth is so stays a judgment.

**Pace.** The condition-level laws of `Becoming.Frequency` give pace for couplings with given strengths. Couplings holding at every step advance a chain one coupling a step (`CoupledAlways.chainInTime`). So a loop of m + 1 of them returns what reached its condition every m + 1 steps (`returns_of_coupledAlways`), and by `carried_returns` each return at least doubles it. After R turns the most difference that can arrive there is at least 2^R times what had reached it (`carried_pow_around`), and likewise at any condition downstream along couplings holding at every step (`carried_pow_downstream`). With the part giving no gap after the start, starting gaps at most D and strengths into each condition at most M, the same amount is at most D·(1 + M)^t whatever the couplings (`carried_le_pow_always`, `carried_le_count` with every step marked). Around such a loop it is exponential both ways (`exponential_around`). Where every listed condition is coupled at every step into every listed condition (`CoupledThroughout`), the lower bound holds from every condition to every condition (`CoupledThroughout.exponential`). The lower bounds are of the carried amount, which a law that takes nothing attains. Under the first law a finite whole to which the rest gives nothing net stays within its stock (`Flow.whole_bounded_of_rest_idle`), so amounts do not grow so without a source beyond.

**The pace of a selection.** `share_rises` compares one generation with the next. Iterated with transmission, carriers leaving at least a offspring and the others at most b, the carriers grow at least as a^n (`carriers_grow`), the others at most as b^n (`others_bounded`), and the ratio of carriers to others at least as (a/b)^n (`share_ratio_pow`). This is the exponential pace of a capture, while the world stays open; enclosed, the descent stops (`Flow.descent_exhausted`).

**Little time.** Under balance, with nothing given to a condition across a stretch, what stands and what has been drawn add up to the starting stock (`Flow.Balances.level_add_drawn`). Where each step's draw exceeds everything drawn before it, as a doubling draw does, more than half the starting stock stands at every step at which the draw is met (`Flow.Balances.half_stands`). Lasting n steps needs a stock of at least 2^n − 1 (`Flow.Balances.doubling_needs`, through `pow_le_drawnBefore`). `DoublingDraw` attains both: draws of 1, 2 and 4 on a stock of 7 leave 4 at the third step and nothing after (`DoublingDraw.half_then_none`). Read with `Web.break_not_bounded`, what stands gives no warning, and doubling the stock buys one step.

**What would change it.** A reading of "entangled" that neither mutual dependence nor its two neighbours captures; a law joining a dependence to a coupling by level with a strength derived, not supplied, which would join the two halves of this item; the pace laws with real strengths or continuous time; a selection whose transmission is noisy.

**Self-review.** The readings are definitions and their order is proved both ways, with witnesses, so the reading is a choice among exact structures and not a verdict encoded in one. The lower bounds hold for every σ, the upper bound for σ = 0, and `exponential_around` states both at σ = 0. `half_stands` uses the first law at the condition: with nothing given, what is taken never exceeds what stands, so "met" is automatic and the law says something about every step of the stretch. No theorem says that mutual dependence makes couplings act; that join is named as supplied.

## 213. Capture through the rule (RC)

```text
Result(s): capture-through-the-rule (new)
Delta: RO's chapter (§8, third row) found that the spine states a selection whose rule holds the
       outcome (Becoming.Capture) and a rule that reads a fast level (Becoming.Pace), but no loop in
       which the rule is read from the share the selection gives. Stated here on Pace's two-level
       course: where no rule turns against the reading, the loop locks at its first reading step;
       where rules can, from a configuration whose rule favours and is not above what the reading
       of its share gives, share and rule fall at no step; a perturbation of the rule that keeps
       its direction is absorbed at the next reading step; a reading that favours at every share
       locks every course from its second reading step, exactly; monotone two-level laws keep the
       order of two courses. Three witnesses show where the proposed statement fails
Supplied premises / correspondence: per statement: the fast step does not lower the share under a
       favouring rule (Raises); the rule read is a monotone function of the share alone
       (ReadsShare); favouring is kept upward. The start condition (Locked), favouring at every share
       (uniform) or favouring at the start are hypotheses of the statements that use them. On
       counts, offspring numbers per carrier and per other; that offspring carry their parents'
       target stays a premise, as in Becoming.Capture
Evidence: Becoming.RuleCapture, 53 theorems, 74 declarations, empty axiom reports; core receipt
          `20261019T151254.157652Z`; connectivity passes on the landing tree, 496 apart of 11,539 theorems, one in Becoming.RuleCapture (`Counts.share_not_lower_counts`, registered as a restatement)
Boundary: that an actual rule reads the share it selects, or reads it monotonically; which readings
          formations live under; real-valued shares and rates; many levels; rules that read more
          than the share
```

RO's map of the Chinese sources onto the spine ([study section 207](#207-the-chinese-sources-on-the-spine-ro)) found three passages, 韩非子's 二柄, 管子·国蓄's 据有余而制不足 and 商君书's 壹赏、壹刑、壹教, whose loop the spine had in parts only. `Becoming.Capture` keeps "the winner shapes the rule" as a reading it does not derive, and `Becoming.Pace` has a rule that reads the fast level, with no share and no selection. RO stated the join it proposed as a gap (`passages.json`, `hanfei-er-bing`), and this item was asked to check it, sharpen it or refute it.

**The question.** In a two-level course whose fast step is a selection and whose rule, read at reading steps, is read from the share the selection gave, do share and rule stop falling? Is a change of the rule alone absorbed, and what leaves the loop?

**The move.** The course is `Pace.paced f h reads`: at every step the fast configuration steps by the rule in force (`f`), and at a reading step the rule becomes what `h` reads from the configuration. Two orders, `Ideals.Preorder`s, carry the comparisons: `P` on fast configurations (`P.le x y`: the share at `y` is not lower than at `x`) and `M` on rules (`M.le g g'`: `g'` favours the carriers at least as much as `g`). `favours` holds of the rules under which selection does not lower the share (`Raises`), and the rule read is monotone in the share alone (`ReadsShare`). The statements are made for every pair of orders, every selection and every reading with these properties, and read on counts (`Counts`: carriers and others, others present), whose share order is the cross-multiplication of `share_not_lower` (`Counts.share_not_lower_counts`). Two lemmas on Pace's course are added: a course read from a later step is the course from its configuration there (`Pace.paced_shift`), and the fast configuration after a step is the selection by the rule in force (`Pace.paced_fast_succ`).

**What is proved** (`Becoming.RuleCapture`).
- **Where no rule turns against the reading** (`favouring_locks`, `favours_throughout`, `Counts.margin_course`, `Counts.rises_strictly`, `Counts.rises_strictly_along`). Where the start's rule and every rule read favour, the share falls at no step from the start, and the course is locked from the step after its first reading step. On counts this is RO's statement with a margin: each carrier leaving `a + m` offspring and each other `a`, the margin read at a reading step a monotone function of the share; from every start under a margin the share falls at no step, and from the step after the first reading step the margin falls at no step. The share rises strictly at every step whose margin is positive, carriers present, along every course.
- **Locked, the loop does not turn back** (`Locked`, `turn_locked`, `locked_stays`, `locked_rises`, `locked_not_below`). Favouring kept by every rule not lower, a configuration whose rule favours and is not above what the reading of its share gives stays locked at every later step, and neither share nor rule falls across any step, reading steps included.
- **Without the start condition, it fails** (`Alternating.alternates`, `Alternating.never_locked`, `Alternating.before_locked`). Under the threshold reading `hi`/`lo` read at every step, from carriers two to one under `lo` (a rule in force against the reading, read one step late), the share falls at every even step and the rule at every odd step, without end, and the course is locked neither way at any step. Its start is the locked configuration `(twoToOne, hi)` with its rule reversed.
- **A perturbation that keeps the direction is absorbed** (`perturbation_invariant`, `perturbation_absorbed`). From a locked configuration, with the rule replaced by any favouring one, above it or below: at the step after every reading step the rule is at least the rule before the perturbation, and the course is locked again. Under margins every perturbation of the margin keeps the direction.
- **A perturbation that reverses it is not** (`Reversed.locked_down`, `Reversed.not_absorbed`). From the same locked configuration, the rule reversed to `lo` and held for one step before the reading: the share crosses the threshold, the course is locked the other way, and neither share nor rule rises again; the rule after the first reading step is below the rule before the perturbation.
- **Leaving** (`favours_after_reading`, `uniform_locks`, `Second.second_exact`). Where the reading favours at every share, every course, whatever its start (share and rule perturbed, a rule against the reading), is locked from the step after its second reading step, and the second is exact: in `Second` the course is not locked at the step after its first reading step and its rule falls across the second. So no change of configuration, share or rule value leaves the lock for longer; what leaves it is a change of the law, of how the rule reads or of the selection. Where the reading favours only above a threshold, a change of configuration across the threshold also leaves (`Reversed.not_absorbed`).
- **Order kept** (`order_kept`, `perturbation_keeps_below`, `Counts.select_mono`, `Counts.perturbation_keeps_below_counts`, `Pace.paced_shift`). Where selection is monotone in the share and in the rule and the reading monotone in the share, two courses keep their order at every step; a perturbation lowering the rule keeps its course below the course without it, on counts under every monotone reading.
- **Counts and their readings** (`Counts.order`, `Counts.select`, `Counts.raises`, `Counts.lowers`, `Counts.upper`, `Counts.lower`, `Counts.proportional`, `Counts.proportional_reads`, `Counts.proportional_locks`, `Counts.proportional_locks_down`, `Counts.threshold`, `Counts.threshold_reads`, `Counts.threshold_favours`, `Counts.margin`, `Counts.byMargin`, `Counts.byMargin_reads`). Selection multiplies each kind by what the rule gives it. Under the proportional reading (each kind's offspring in proportion to how many of its kind there are), from a rule that favours and is not above the population's own proportion the carriers' share and the rule fall at no step; from one that disfavours and is not below it, they rise at none. A threshold reading is monotone where its lower rule is not above its upper one, and favours at every share where both favour.

**Where RO's statement holds and where it does not.** RO's gap takes the margin as a natural number, so no rule disfavours, and in that model its claims (i) and (ii) hold, stronger than stated: the share falls at no step and, from the step after the first reading step, the margin falls at no step, not only at reading steps (`Counts.margin_course`); strictly where the margin is positive (`Counts.rises_strictly_along`). Its claim (iii), that a change of the margin alone is re-absorbed at the next reading step, holds there for every perturbation of the margin, since every one keeps the direction (`perturbation_absorbed`). Where rules can favour the others, (i) and (ii) need the start condition `Locked` (`Alternating` refutes them without it), (iii) holds exactly for perturbations that keep the direction (`Reversed` refutes it for one that reverses), and the claim that leaving needs a change of `h` holds where the reading favours at every share (`uniform_locks`); under a threshold reading, a change of configuration across the threshold also leaves.

**What this changes.** In a loop whose rule reads the share it selects, the outcome is held by how the rule reads, not by the rule's value: every reading step sets the value again from the share. This is the mirror of `Law.perturbation_reabsorbed`, where the state is re-absorbed because the next step does not read it; here the rule's value is re-set because the reading does not read it, and the share, which the reading does read, carries the loop. The chapter's "a counter-loop has to reach the rule" (§4) is sharpened to: where the rule is read from the share it selects, it has to reach how the rule reads. That a rule reads the share it selects, monotonically, is the premise `ReadsShare`: it is where "the winner shapes the rule" of `Becoming.Capture` enters, now as a stated hypothesis, and what is derived is that such a rule holds the outcome.

*Readings* [AI reading, D57]. 二柄's 「今君人者释其刑德而使臣用之，则君反制于臣矣」 reads the rule of selection read from the share of those it selects: locked, the loop does not turn back. 韩非 reads the loop as control between opposed interests, and that divergence is kept. 据有余而制不足 is read by the proportional reading: the kind holding more is favoured and holds more (`Counts.proportional_locks`). 壹赏、壹刑、壹教 is one reading favouring one way at every share; every course is locked from its second reading step, and only a change of how the rule reads leaves (`uniform_locks`). RO's passage map carries the three readings ([D57](DELEGATED-CHOICES.md#d57-经由规则的捕获之读--the-readings-of-capture-through-the-rule)).

**Not done.** Real-valued shares and rates; rules that read more than the share (the share and the rule in force, a history of shares); many levels; noisy or delayed readings beyond one step; whether an actual rule reads the share it selects; a join with RG's two-sided regulation once it lands; an independent review.

**Self-review.** The statements were read against the Lean.
- `Locked` is `favours p.2 ∧ M.le p.2 (h p.1 p.2)`: the rule in force favours and is not above what the reading gives. `turn_locked` proves both cases of a turn (reading or not) keep it, using `upper` for the read rule and `monotone` on the risen share; `locked_rises` is stated across every step, so reading steps are included.
- `perturbation_absorbed` takes the perturbed rule `g'` with only `favours g'` and states the bound against the pre-perturbation rule `g`, at the step after every reading step `r` (any `r`, not only the first); the invariant carries `M.le g (h …)` along all steps before.
- `uniform_locks` needs two reading steps `r < r'`: after `r` every rule favours (`favours_after_reading`), and at `r'` the read rule is above the one in force; `Second.second_exact` shows one reading step is not enough, with the reading favouring at every share.
- `Counts.order.trans` cancels the middle count with `Nat.le_of_mul_le_mul_right` and its positivity, which is why `Counts` keeps others present; commutation is by Capture's `mul_assoc_nat` and two local lemmas (`Counts.mul_right_comm_nat`, `Counts.mul_mul_mul_comm_nat`), since the prelude's `Nat.mul_assoc` and `Nat.mul_left_comm` use `propext`.
- `Alternating` reads at every step; its even and odd steps are computed through `course_step`, and `never_locked` checks both orders at both parities. `Reversed` reads from step 1 on; its course from step 1 is locked in the reversed orders, through `ReadsShare.reverse`.
- `Counts.share_not_lower_counts` restates `share_not_lower` in the share order; it is registered apart as a restatement, and every other law of the module is read on courses.
- The module imports `Becoming.Pace` and `Becoming.Ideals`; every declaration has an empty axiom report (scratch build and core receipt).

## 214. A level held from both sides, and a level read late (RG)

```text
Result(s): two-sided-regulation-and-late-reading (new)
Delta: the law of restoration (Flow.restores, Becoming.Continuation) has one side: where the
       exchange gives more than it takes below m, the level reaches at least m. RO's passage map
       (study section 207; chapter CHINESE-SOURCES-AND-BECOMING section 8, first gap) found no law
       for a level held from both sides, nor for one held by a rule reading the level late, and
       AssurancePlans.Regulation has two levels and an immediate response. Becoming.Regulation
       proves both: the bound on the exchange is exactly no overshoot; within it and opposing on
       both sides the level settles at m within its gap; beyond it the level crosses m, and a
       witness oscillates without end; one side alone can leave the level away for ever; a rule
       reading l steps late needs a band of at least 2 (l + 1) d, which the late return attains;
       the late relay goes l M past its entry, and every start held below its band settles exactly
       where a + (l + 1) M <= b + 1, else the start held at a - 1 leaves both ends without end
Supplied premises / correspondence: none beyond each law's hypotheses (balance at the condition,
       the bound, opposition, a rule reading l late, a rest within d a step, a step M, a band
       [a, b]); reading 损有余而补不足, 冲气以为和, 济其不及以泄其过 and 中节 as these laws is the
       AI's (the passage map, below)
Evidence: Becoming.Regulation, 108 theorems, 136 declarations, empty axiom reports; core
          receipt `20261019T152617.511553Z`; connectivity check passes, 495 apart of 11,647, none in the
          module; one register entry removed (Becoming.gap_le_iff, now used on the base);
          simulate.py's seven checks, run before the proofs, agree with every statement
Boundary: one condition read at a time; the relay's threshold is the relay's alone; one policy
          keeping a band from every start in it, and the lumping of several regulated levels into
          one, are not proved
```

Board item RG, the first gap RO found (chapter [中国思想与生成](../../../../theories/becoming/chapters/CHINESE-SOURCES-AND-BECOMING.md) section 8, first row): passages 老子 77 (天之道损有馀而补不足, and 张弓: 高者抑之，下者举之), 老子 42 (冲气以为和), 左传 昭公二十年 (济其不及以泄其过; 宽猛相济) and 中庸 (中和). The spine had the one-sided law of restoration (`Flow.restores`) and the excess laws of `Becoming.Continuation`, and `AssurancePlans.Regulation`, a two-level model whose response is immediate. New core module [`Becoming.Regulation`](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/Regulation.lean), after `Becoming.Continuation` and `Becoming.Propagation`, prelude-only. The statements were checked by simulation before the proofs ([simulate.py](../history/root-foundation/development/rg-regulation/simulate.py)).

**The question.** What holds of a level at one condition when the joint exchange there opposes its departure from `m` on both sides (`Flow.Opposes`: taking more than giving above `m`, giving more than taking below), and what changes when the rule fixing the exchange reads the level late?

**(1) The bound is exactly no overshoot.** With balance across a step, the joint exchange departs from evenness by at most the level's gap to `m` on each side (`Flow.WithinGap`) exactly where the next level lies between `m` and the present one (`Flow.withinGap_iff_between`, from the arithmetic `Regulation.within_iff_between`). The bound is not an extra premise of good behaviour: it is the statement that the step does not cross `m`, read off balance. For an opposing exchange the three cases are exact (`Flow.withinGap_iff_of_above`, `Flow.withinGap_iff_of_below`, `Flow.withinGap_iff_of_at`), and beyond the bound the level crosses (`Flow.crosses_of_above`, `Flow.crosses_of_below`).

**(2) Two-sided regulation, and its two failures.** Within the gap, the gap does not rise and the level never crosses `m` (`Flow.gap_le_of_within`, `Flow.stays_between_at`); within it and opposing, the gap falls by at least one at every step where it is positive (`Flow.gap_falls`), by `n` over `n` steps (`Flow.regulates_at`, `Flow.regulates`), and the level is `m` from the step its gap is used up on (`Flow.settles_at`, `Flow.settles_from`, `Flow.settles`). From below, the law of restoration with the bound reaches `m` exactly and stays (`Flow.restores_exactly`). Both failures are witnessed. `Regulation.Overshooting` balances, opposes the departure at every step and exceeds the gap at every step; its level alternates between `2` and `0` about `m = 1` and is never `1` (`Overshooting.oscillates`, `Overshooting.never_at`). `Regulation.OneSided` meets the premise of the law of restoration from every step and the bound at every step, does not oppose the departure above `m`, and stays above `m` (`OneSided.restores_premise`, `OneSided.not_opposes`, `OneSided.above`).

**(3) The band a late reading needs.** A rule reads `ℓ` steps late (`Regulation.ReadsLate`) where what it gives and takes at a step is fixed by the rest's record up to `ℓ + 1` steps before; it may keep anything it has read, its own exchanges included. A flow follows a rule at a condition where its joint exchange is the rule's plus the rest's (`Flow.FollowsRule`). Two rests agreeing before `T` get the same exchanges from the rule up to step `T + ℓ` (`ReadsLate.alike`) and leave the same levels up to `T` (`Regulation.levels_alike`); the levels at `T + ℓ + 1` differ by exactly what the rests exchange differently over the `ℓ + 1` steps from `T` (`Regulation.late_spread`). With one rest raising by `d` and the other lowering by `d` over the window, no band `[a, b]` holding both is narrower than `2 (ℓ + 1) d` (`Regulation.late_band`); on the course a rule generates from a start `x₀` above `0`, no rule reading `ℓ` late keeps the level within `[a, b]` under every rest moving it by at most `d` a step unless `a + 2 (ℓ + 1) d ≤ b` (`Regulation.no_narrower_band`). The late return (`Regulation.lateReturn`) moves back at each step what the rest exchanged `ℓ + 1` steps before; it reads `ℓ` late (`lateReturn_readsLate`), and needs only the level read `ℓ` steps late and its own exchanges (`lateReturn_reads_levels`). It keeps every course within `(ℓ + 1) d` of its start (`lateReturn_keeps`), and where `(ℓ + 1) d ≤ x₀` its course balances and stays in the band of width exactly `2 (ℓ + 1) d` about `x₀` (`lateReturn_band`). The least band is attained.

**(4) The late relay.** The relay (`Regulation.relay`) gives a step `M` for a reading below `a`, takes `M` for a reading above `b` and does neither within `[a, b]`; a flow relays `ℓ` late (`Flow.RelaysLate`) where it does so for the level `ℓ` steps before. Readings below drive pushes, above pulls, within rests (`push_ramp`, `pull_ramp`, `rest_ramp`); a level entering the band after `ℓ` readings below goes on by exactly `ℓ M` (`overshoot`, `undershoot`), and the relay's own rise or fall, read late, feeds itself (`rise_run`, `fall_run`). From a start held below `a` for its first `ℓ + 1` steps the level rises by `M` a step (`held_rise`) and enters within one step of `a`; it settles in the band where the entry carried `ℓ M` further is within `b` (`held_settles`) and passes `b` otherwise (`held_leaves`). An upward crossing (`Web.UpCrossing`: an entry within one step of `a` that passes `b` when carried `ℓ M` further) is followed by a downward one (`Web.DownCrossing`), and that by an upward one (`upCrossing_next`, `downCrossing_next`, `upCrossing_later`): each entry is within one step of the end it enters at, so each overshoot passes the other end, and after every step the level is somewhere above `b` and somewhere below `a` (`crossing_oscillates`). The start held at `a - 1` crosses exactly where `b + 2 ≤ a + (ℓ + 1) M` (`held_crosses`, `held_oscillates`), and every start held below `a` settles where `a + (ℓ + 1) M ≤ b + 1` (`held_below_settles`). The relay has a run from every start where `(ℓ + 1) M ≤ b + 1`: its window law (`relayWindow`) iterated by `Law.orbit` gives a flow and web that relay `ℓ` late, balance at every step and hold the start for `ℓ + 1` steps (`relay_runs`). So the threshold is exact: for `0 < a ≤ b`, `0 < M` and `(ℓ + 1) M ≤ b + 1`, every run from every start held below the band settles in it exactly where `a + (ℓ + 1) M ≤ b + 1` (`relay_threshold`).

**What RO proposed and what is proved.** The board row stated three claims.

- (1) Proved as stated, and sharper: the bound is exactly no overshoot (an equivalence, not a sufficient condition), and from below the level reaches `m` exactly (`restores_exactly`).
- (2) Proved for a fixed start `x₀`, with `0 < a` so the course's levels stay positive and balance, and `(ℓ + 1) d ≤ x₀` for the late return to balance. The proposal's "whatever it keeps" holds: `ReadsLate` constrains only what the exchange is a function of, and the rule may keep its own past exchanges.
- (3) Proved for a start held below the band: the entry goes on `ℓ M` (`overshoot`); it settles exactly where entry plus `ℓ M` stays in the band; once it leaves, it goes beyond both ends without end; the start held at `a - 1` leaves exactly where `(ℓ + 1) M ≥ b - a + 2`. Sharper: the threshold for every start held below is `a + (ℓ + 1) M ≤ b + 1`, and the relay's runs exist under the stated floor.

RO's gap for 左传 昭公二十年 named three statements (i)–(iii). (iii) is proved exactly (above). (i) is proved for one start, the rule chosen with it: under every rest within `d` a step, no rule reading `ℓ` late keeps a band narrower than `2 (ℓ + 1) d`, and the late return keeps that band. One policy keeping `[a, b]` from every start in it is not proved. (ii), the lumping of several regulated levels read as one, is not proved.

**The passage map.** [build_passages.py](development/ro-relational-sources/build_passages.py) now carries what a board item proved of a gap (`RESOLVED`). It adds declarations and records, replaces or adds the sentences of the reading that named the gap, and keeps the gap's own statement with what was proved beside it. It never removes a declaration or record the mappers gave. For RG: 老子 77 and 老子 42 cite the two-sided laws and their failures; 左传 昭公二十年 cites the late band, the relay's overshoot, its endless crossing and its exact threshold; 中庸 中和 adds a reading of 中节 as a response within the gap, which is the AI's. `verify_ro.py` passes on the landing receipt, and the passage tables of the chapter are regenerated from the map.

**Not derived.** That a given system regulates, how late it reads, or the size of its step: each is a named premise of the laws that use it. The modelling choices are the spine's: discrete steps, whole-number amounts, one condition read at a time, and the rest's record a pair of amounts a step. No ethical predicate, ranking or axiom occurs. That holding a level is good is not stated; the laws say what holds it and how wide a band it needs.

**What would change it.** A law of one policy keeping a band from every start in it under late reading; the lumping of several regulated levels; regulation with amounts in a field, where a factor below one closes gradually (`Becoming.Widening`'s open item); a relay with dead time differing by side.

<a id="215-the-refutation-laws-hold-however-a-family-is-listed-r23"></a>
## 215. The refutation laws hold however a family is listed (R23)

```text
Result(s): listing-once-is-decided-identity (advanced; its next delta closed)
Delta: P77 (section 101) classed 30 uses of Distinct in the core as free (F0): the law's other
       hypotheses read its family through membership only, and its conclusion is a refutation,
       so not_of_listsOnce discharges listing once. Six were proved as corollaries. The new core
       module Becoming.ListingRefutations proves the other 22 laws of the five modules the
       inventory names, each as a `_listing` corollary with no Distinct; fifteen need no decided
       identity either, and the seven whose law's statement takes [DecidableEq] on its type (the
       fed-from-beyond and boundary laws) keep that instance;
       the remaining two F0 rows (Frontier.frontier, Lone.frontier) are laws inside witnesses
       whose lists are without repetition by construction and need no corollary.
Premises: none beyond each law's own; statements of existing theorems unchanged.
Output → input: chapter section 8.2 (Listing, counting and decidedness) loses the item; the
       reading of 生生之謂易 (Web.generation_fed_from_beyond) holds of a family however listed.
```

**What was proved.** `Becoming.ListingRefutations` imports `Listing` and `Standpoints` and adds nothing else. Membership lemmas first: balance on a family, being fed from beyond it and the boundary of its region as a cut are matters of its members (`Flow.BalancesOn.of_same`, `Flow.FedFromBeyond.of_within`, `Flow.cut_of_same`); a stock that is nothing over a family is nothing over every family with no other members, and so is its product with a refinement (`Web.stock_zero_of_within`, `mul_zero_of`, from `total_zero_of_within`). Then the corollaries:
- `Becoming.Continuation`: `Flow.fed_from_beyond_listing`, `Flow.fed_from_beyond_from_listing`, `Flow.rising_fed_from_beyond_listing`, `Flow.rising_fed_from_beyond_from_listing`, `Web.generation_fed_from_beyond_listing`;
- `Becoming.Dissipation`: `Flow.More.opens_listing`, `Flow.opens_of_arising_listing`, `Flow.rising_opens_listing`, `Flow.standing_opens_listing`, `Flow.rise_alone_opens_listing`, `Flow.taking_draws_in_from_listing`, `Flow.rising_draws_in_from_listing`, `Flow.rising_draws_in_listing`, `Flow.standing_draws_in_listing`, and, where some list with repetition allowed holds every condition, `Flow.rising_not_recurring_listing` and `Flow.standing_not_recurring_listing` (the inventory's `rising_ceases` and `standing_ceases`, renamed since);
- `Becoming.Resolution`: `Flow.taking_needs_refinement_listing`;
- `Becoming.Roles`: `Web.generation_opens_listing`, `Web.generation_draws_in_from_listing`, `Web.generation_draws_in_listing`;
- `Becoming.Standpoints`: `Flow.boundary_crossed_listing`, `Flow.region_not_a_cut_listing`.

Each proof is the same two steps the inventory named: `not_of_listsOnce` on the family, and the transport of every hypothesis and of the refuted claim along the members (`Around.of_same`, `Inward.of_same`, `ClosedAt.widen`, `takers_pos_of_sub` and the lemmas above). 28 theorems, empty axiom reports.

**What it changes.** The laws whose conclusion is a refutation now hold, as stated corollaries, of every family however listed: a family may list a member twice, and, except in the seven laws whose own statement takes `[DecidableEq]` on the type, nothing need tell its members apart. Listing once remains a local condition only where a law sums or counts once per member (the inventory's L and K classes, and `Doubled.needs_once` shows the sum law fails over a repeated list). Four laws of `Continuation` and the two of `Standpoints` assumed `DecidableEq` as well; their corollaries keep it, since the laws they rest on take it, though no corollary uses it to list the family.

**Not derived.** No count or sum law becomes free; the corollaries add no reading.

<a id="217-the-stepwise-classes-and-loss-r27"></a>
## 217. The stepwise classes and loss (R27)

```text
Result(s): significance-retained-within-margin (advanced)
Delta: the twentieth review (D2, F13) found that no theorem relates the order on what can form
       (Includes, Widens, Retains) to the stepwise classes of an event (within renewal,
       undermining), the one theorem relating them being a divergence
       (Preemption.not_undermining_yet_loses). Becoming.Significance now states both directions:
       levels below a need are exceeded by every path admitting the formation there
       (Web.exceeded_of_below); an undermining event, through dependences on its condition holding
       across the step at no smaller need, leaves the levels exceeded by every path meeting those
       dependences after the step (Web.UnderminingOn.exceeded), so keeping what can form excludes
       undermining there (Web.Includes.not_undermining), and from a standpoint at which those
       continuations have significance nothing is retained (Web.UnderminingOn.not_retains; under
       the continuation condition from every standpoint, .not_retains_unrestricted); the converse
       fails, the preempting drawer's event being within renewal and not undermining while its part
       closes a possibility (Preemption.within_renewal_yet_loses).
Premises: the dependences on the undermined condition hold across the step at no smaller need,
       and the compared path meets them after the step; for significance, that those continuations
       have significance from the standpoint. No balance or flow premise: the laws read one web.
Output → input: the stepwise classes read the order on what can form in one direction; together
       with the margin law (loss exactly where the net draw passes the margin) this is the relation
       D2 asked for. The reading "generative at the level of formations = renewing" is not a
       theorem: renewal is no sign of keeping.
```

**Why both premises.** Undermining compares the level after the step with the need *at* the step; admission after the step reads the need after it. Where a dependence weakens or dissolves across the step, the formation may be admitted after it although the level fell, so the theorem asks that the dependence hold at no smaller need. Where the compared path does not meet the dependence after the step (a part that only shares a fall others cause), the levels with the part are not shown to lose anything, so the theorem asks that it does; with the path the levels without a part, this is the margin law's condition read at one condition and one step.

**What it does not show.** Nothing about consuming or arising (the whole-run classes): a run's consuming a condition is read over its whole course, while inclusion compares two paths at every step, and no law here relates them. Whether a part that undermines also adds elsewhere (mixed) is not decided: the laws show only that the levels with it do not include the levels without it.

**Records.** [`rebind.py`](development/r28-one-base/rebind.py) moves the declarations that changed file to the record's reference to their new file (`Dependence`, `WebAt` → World.lean; `Law.process`, `Branching.Reachable`, `KeepsPossibilities`, `Returns`, `Lossless`, `Merges`, `units_length`, `law_trace_of`, `law_trace_iff`, `law_reach_iff` → Recurrence.lean), checking each against the receipt's elaborated declarations; rebinds proof bindings to the changed Lean files; re-points references to the changed files where the record was current, after reading the change; and adds a history note: 193 records changed, 21 of them with a moved declaration. `worlds-are-runs` gains the declarations that make a world a run by its type and loses the boundary "worlds are still defined without processes", now shown; its next step is the laws over every law of exchange.

**Self-review.** The change is definitional: every statement keeps its meaning and, but for that one spelling, its text, and the eight new theorems are `rfl` lemmas or the old bridges read the other way. `Law.Lossless` and the others now mean the process form at `Law.process next`, equivalent to the old orbit form by the unfolding lemmas; a reader of a statement about `Law.Lossless next` reads the same proposition up to that equivalence, which is now a theorem rather than a definition. `World.history` is a structure field, so the receipt lists `World` rather than a declaration of that name; records name `World.web`, `World.flow` and `World.of`. What is not done here, by S4's scope: the `Law.*` theorems with a `Branching.*` twin stay (R29), the companion modules stay (R32), Interleavings does not yet construct the `World` (R33), and the measure's new class for companion modules is R32's.

**What changed in the Lean.** Theorems 11,684 → 11,658, modules 298 → 299 (Amounts added), audited declarations 15,976 → 15,949. - `Switching.no_state_law_of_criterion` (LawAlongRun) is removed for `Switching.no_state_law` (Mechanism).

- `Hexagram.pairs_goAlike_of_commutes` (Commuting) is removed for `Hexagram.pairs_goAlike` (Hexagrams).
- `Remainder.carriedWithin_exact` and `…_of_no_loop` are removed for the names of Loops.
- `ExchangeLaw.Nonanticipating.through_sensitive_of_every` (Sensitivity) is removed for `ExchangeLaw.Nonanticipating.through_sensitive` (Counterfactual).
- In ReferencePlan, where both names were in one module, the old names `added_keeps`, `new_contact_choice` and `trace_conserves` carry the proofs through the laws, and the `_of_law` names are removed.
- `Hexagram.complement_line`, `flip_line` and `or_false_split` are removed for `line_complement`, `line_flip_self` and `neither` (HexagramPlaces). `neither` moved there from HexagramLaws, the common ancestor.

The second proofs through the general laws are therefore no longer named theorems. The connection is a docstring line, as the review proposed. No name OPENING's body cites was removed. `Law.lost_stays`, which the RO passages and the chapter cite, stays as a one-line case.

**Not done, and why (G8).** The decided counting laws of Counting (`counting_free`, `counting_under`, `premised_counting`, `counting_binds_iff`, `enclosure_bounds_change` and the enclosed and finite families) do not become corollaries of CensusCounts' counted forms. Only their forward direction, from the tally to every decided world, follows from a counted form: by `CountsHold.obey` at worlds with decidable activity, a proof already of about five lines. The converse cannot follow. The counted hypothesis quantifies over every world meeting the selection, the decided one only over worlds with decidable activity, so both converses need the witness queues and rings. So does `counting_binds_iff`'s forward direction.

Putting the counted forms below would need Counting to import Decidedness (there is no cycle) and CensusCounts' 41 theorems to be interleaved through Counting's 4,630 lines. `counting_under` alone has 11 dependents in Counting's binding sections, and 38 declarations depend on the twelve laws. That restructure would save the five-line forward proofs and no witness. A shared witness lemma (B11's one census table), from which both converses are short, is the compression this item needs. It changes no statement and belongs with B11.

**Text.** The following follow R29:
- `Becoming.lean`: the import, and the notes of Amounts, LeastLoss and SelectionPool.
- The checker's `CORE` list (Amounts before LeastLoss) and its `SCOPE` text. No logic changed.

- OPENING's footnote [^conditions], which is AI-written: it cites `Becoming.Amounts` and the rest theorem `World.rests_unrefuted_enclosed`, proved from the law. The body, in Ren's voice, is unchanged.

**Checks.** Core receipt `20261019T185632.962707Z` (Lean 4.29.1, main `87ecfdee5` with R29 in the working tree) passed:
- 299 core modules and 11,658 theorems; every core declaration's axiom report is empty.
- The core compiles from the prelude.
- 1,043 Lean steps ran and 165 were reused.

The connectivity measure on the same sources counts 489 of 11,658 apart (485 of 11,684 before). The families are unchanged: World reaches Process, and Process, Flow and Web reach neither. 866 statements are on both families.

The two whole-number restatements were register entries, and their entries moved to [`apart-retired.json`](development/r29-compression/apart-retired.json). Four theorems whose only user was a removed second name are now apart roots, registered with reasons by [`apart.py`](development/r29-compression/apart.py): `Dependence.level_registers`, `unrefuted_falls_exceed`, `ExchangeLaw.Nonanticipating.readsFinitely_of_every` and `no_chain_of_no_loop_listed`.

**Records.** [`rebind.py`](development/r29-compression/rebind.py) reads the moves and removals off the two receipts and checks that every removal has a kept name. It then:

204 records changed, 25 of them with a moved or replaced declaration.

**Self-review.** The compression keeps every kept statement's type, and the receipt checks each one. It removes 26 theorems and one definition. The cost is that some links are now docstring lines and no longer named theorems:


**The table.** [RENAME-TABLE.json](development/r30-names/RENAME-TABLE.json) lists each applied row (old, new, kind, reason, and the decision where the row was medium) and each row judged and left, with why. Its `declarations`, `modules`, `paths` and `namespaces` maps are what other tools read; `text_windows`, `text_words` and `text_backticked` are the rules for prose. It was generated by `gen.py` on R29's core, decided by `decide.py`, and applied by `apply.py` (names resolved through the namespace stack, the `open` lines and the import closure, dot notation by the type of the receiver), `positive.py` and `manual.py` (32 exact edits of code and docstrings). Every removed name and every added one was read off the two receipts: the names in R29's receipt and not in R30's are exactly the table's old names, and the new ones exactly its new names.

The groups:
- **Returns, the other senses.** `Web.Returns` and `ReturnsWithin` (a dependence met again) are `Web.Restored` and `RestoredWithin`, in the module `Restoration`. Frequency's root `Returns` (a loop's round trip, which shadowed `Branching.Returns` wherever Branching is open) is `RoundTrip`. `Law.Returns` and `Branching.Returns`, the configuration sense, keep the name.
- **Lossless, the amount sense.** `Flow.Lossless` and `LosslessOn` (conserved amounts) are `Flow.Conserving` and `ConservingOn`, beside `Branching.Lossless` (injective steps); `Flow.history`, a number, is `Flow.exchangeCount`.
- **Settles and Rests.** `HistoryIdeals.Settles` is `HasLongest`, `Stretches.Settles` is `HasLatest`. `Learnable.RestsFrom` and `Rests` (and LearnableRuns') are `PredictsFrom` and `Predicts`: nothing in the definition rests; the prediction is right from T on. `World.RestsFrom` (停息), `Enough.RestsFrom`, `Enough.Rests` and `Enough.Settles` keep their names, since D42 and D45(4) stand: an extrapolation or seeking that comes to rest settles with the target met.
- **generation.** The word is kept for 生生 (widening; generation and degeneration do not overlap). `Web.generation_*` are `Web.embodiedArising_*` (each says embodied members arise at arbitrarily late steps), `Web.Regenerating` is `Web.ActiveRenewer` (the draft's `Replenishing` is a witness namespace of Rejoining), `ExchangeLaw.generation` is `ExchangeLaw.process`, `SharedCodes.generation` is `nextCohort`, `ResponseLearning`'s `*generation*` are `*cohort*`, and `contingent_generation*` and `Handoff.generation_by_bound*` are `newContent`.
- **The ethics names.** `G0` is `LivingSignificance` and the `g0_*` are `livingSignificance_*`; `Valuation.SelfGood` and `ProfileReach.SelfGood` are `SelfSignificance`; `SecuresPositiveGround` is `SecuresNewContent` (content absent before, no valence); `PositiveGround` (module and namespace) is `SecuredContent`; `Clearing.free_rider_loses` is `Clearing.clearer_loses_dweller`, which says what the theorem proves.
- **Other wrong meanings and collisions.** `Coupling` (module and namespace) is `MoveFormation`; `Onward.DependentSelection` is `DependentChoice`; `Joining.Neutral` is `TwoSidedUnit` (beside `Becoming.Neutral`, boundary neutrality); `RuleCapture.Counts` is `CarrierCounts` and `Countdown.Counts` is `CountedWork` (the root `Counts` stays); `SharedCodes.Image` is `Relabels`; `Activation.History` is `TwoSteps`; `Registration.History` is `AlikeUpTo`; `ReferencePlan.Alike` and `Contacts.Alike` are `AgreeOn`; `Ideals.Closed` is `ScottClosed`.

**Dropped, and why.** Five borderline groups are kept: `Narrowing.Settles` ("settles a question" is idiomatic, no collision in use), `GuardHorizon.Closed` (local, and its theorem already reads `closed_viable`), the witness `Generations` (the lineage sense is exact), Slowing's `phase_*_return` names (they name an event of the witness) and `Branching.Keeps` (local, no collision). The 32 rows the draft judged not justified are kept as it said (the other `Keeps`, `Closed`, `Continues`, `Balanced`, the course and history sequences, `Web.static` and its lemmas).

**The Unfolding sites (left for R34).** The 28 uses of the `Unfolding` record in the core (Ranking 19, Relevance 5, ActiveReading 4) are not ported. A port changes the parameter `U : W → Unfolding F C` to a `Web`, which changes what the statement quantifies over, and `Renewed`, `Dependent` and `ConsumingIn` to their `Web.static_*` forms; none is a few lines with the meaning unchanged. R34 restates these modules (`Pos := F`) and takes them.

**OPENING and the chain.** OPENING's body names no renamed declaration; its footnotes `[^good-evil]`, `[^aligned]` and `[^collective]` (`Clearing.clearer_loses_dweller`) and `[^present]` (`runaway_of_roundTrip`) follow the table. GENERATIVITY-CHAIN names none. Nothing is left for a proposal.

**Checks.** Core receipt `20261019T194851.524223Z` (Lean 4.29.1, main `4cc010fb0` with R30 in the working tree) passed: 299 core modules, 11,658 theorems and 15,949 audited declarations, as in R29; every core declaration's axiom report is empty; the core compiles from the prelude; 1,069 Lean steps ran and 139 were reused. [`sigcheck.py`](development/r30-names/sigcheck.py) compares every declaration's type as the checker's Signatures steps print it: all 7,650 entries agree after renaming by the table and the binder (36 of them through dot notation, `W.Returns c` now `W.Restored c`). [`verify_ro.py`](development/ro-relational-sources/verify_ro.py) and the Y1 map's [`verify_mapping.py`](development/y1-changes/verify_mapping.py) pass on the receipt.

**Text.** By [`text.py`](development/r30-names/text.py), N5's rule (a qualified name anywhere; inside backticks also a last component every declaration of which is renamed to one name; prose words not touched): the chapter (en, zh), the reference catalogue, the chapters on the Chinese sources and on the 易传, G0-WARRANT and WISDOM-AND-CONTEXT (en, zh), the Lean READMEs (with the bare module names of the import order), DELEGATED-CHOICES, MODULE-CLASSIFICATION and DECIDABILITY-INVENTORY (en, zh). The chapter's glossary has a table of the retired Lean names of 20 October (en, zh), and §9's receipt paragraph follows R30. The RO map is rebuilt by `build_passages.py`, whose renames after FIXES now take the R30 table (each so corrected passage says so); its chapter tables are written by `verify_ro.py`'s own table function. The Y1 map, which has no build, is renamed from its R29 bytes by [`y1_names.py`](development/r30-names/y1_names.py). Older studies, reviews, sources and receipts keep the old names as history.

**Records.** [`rebind.py`](development/r30-names/rebind.py) renames the live fields of every record by the table (a declaration entry by its full name; text by the rule above and, outside backticks, by a one-component name that cannot be an English word; record IDs are stable and do not change), moves paths and binding pointers with the module renames, rebinds the proof bindings to the changed Lean files, re-points current references after reading the change and adds a history note. Aliases follow the new names, as in N5: the registry requires an alias to be an elaborated declaration of the bound receipt.

**What changed in the Lean.** Theorems 11,658 → 11,566, modules 299 → 305, audited declarations 15,949 → 15,857. The 92 fewer theorems are the 111 removed copies less the 19 names the prelude gives in its own namespaces where no kept name existed. The kit is [`development/r31-support/`](development/r31-support/). Per item:

- **The ethics out of the general import closure (A4, A12).** `Significance` 39 → 16, `Interdependence` 30 → 25, `Feedback` 102 → 95, `ValuationFrames` 33 → 23, `Continuation` 53 → 47 and `Regions` 26 → 20 give their theorems that take no condition to `Retaining` (21: retaining and adding for any significance, the margin theorems, the stepwise classes, `Preemption`), `Clearing` (14: the witness and its facts on admission, regions and retaining) and `Extension` (10: C on frames and on level paths, with no valuation), and their conditional theorems where bounded significance meets the condition to `BoundedSignificance` (12). `Flow.Balances.comparison_within_reach` (Feedback) and `Trophic.responsive_comparison` (Response) are now proved with no condition, their statements unchanged. [`graph.py`](development/r31-support/graph.py) measures the closure. Before, 138 of 298 core modules reached `Metaethics` or `Significance` through their imports, 17 of them naming the condition or a valuation and 121 not. After, 20 of 304 do, 16 naming it. The four that reach it without naming it (`ActiveReading`, `BoundaryWorlds`, `Ranking`, `ScoreRepresentation`) read `LivingSignificance` or the boundaries of `Boundaries` and are left for a later item. The facts of `Clearing` that read feeding, reach or the boundaries stay in `Feedback`, `Interdependence`, `MutualDependence` and `Boundaries`.
- **One law module (A7).** [`laws_module.py`](development/r31-support/laws_module.py) moves `Determined` (from Joint), the laws of change and partial laws (from Assurance), `GoAlikeUnder` (from Likeness) and `GoAlike` (from Mechanism) into `Becoming.Laws`, after the frame. `GoAlike P π` is now `GoAlikeUnder P π Eq`, which unfolds to the old body; every type that mentions it prints as before. So `Assurance` imports `Laws`, not `Joint`. The two imports of a higher layer that §9 recorded (`Assurance` on `Joint`, `Lasting` on `Likeness`) are no longer exceptions: the first is gone, and with computed layers `Lasting` and `Likeness` are both L1. `DependsOnlyOn` is not an instance of `GoAlikeUnder` and stays in Mechanism; `Reachable`, `Invariant` and `Feasible` were already in the frame.
- **One prelude (A9, B12, B6, G15).** [`prelude.py`](development/r31-support/prelude.py) builds `Becoming.Prelude` from Naturals (18), ListTests (36), the root arithmetic of Dependence and OneStep, and the lemmas of truth values, options and lists that modules re-proved. [`dedup-table.json`](development/r31-support/dedup-table.json) has 59 groups: 39 keep a moved name, 19 a new name in `Naturals` or `ListTests`, and in one (`IntegerOrder.sub_self`) the kept name stays in Integers. A group lists only copies whose explicit and implicit arguments come in the order of the kept name, so a use is renamed and nothing else changes. The 492 renamed uses are logged in `prelude.log.tsv`. `Integers` and `IntegerOrder` stay. No name that OPENING, the chapter or the RO and Y1 maps cite was removed. Records name removed copies only in declaration lists and in one sentence (how-often-couplings-act: `Closing.ble_false_of_lt` is now `Naturals.ble_false_of_lt`).
- **Order split (B15).** [`split_order.py`](development/r31-support/split_order.py) cuts Order.lean along its readings: `Stuttering` (79 theorems: steps at which nothing happens), `Reordering` (173: exchanges taken in the other order, the order as an object, the converse) and `IdleRemoval` (13). Each part is moved unchanged with its declarations and their order, and each module's doc is the part of Order's doc on it. One theorem of Order was a copy (266 → 265). OneStep's arithmetic support is in the prelude (OneStep 311 → 306).
- **Layers (A5).** [`layers.py`](development/r31-support/layers.py) computes a module's layer from its source and imports. L0 is World, Frame and Prelude. L2 is a module whose source, outside comments and imports, names `Unrestricted` or `Valuation`, or that imports such a module. L1 is the rest. It checks that no module imports a higher layer. The counts are L0 3, L1 280 and L2 21 (17 naming, 4 importing). It writes the README module table (304 rows) and its Chinese edition (118 rows, the modules it had and R31's), with each row's description kept. It also writes the sentence after each table, which replaces the README's hand sentence, and the layer tags and new notes in `Becoming.lean`, which now imports every core module. The chapter's §9 points to the generated table. [`chapter_zh_table.py`](development/r31-support/chapter_zh_table.py) retags the Chinese chapter's table with the computed layers and the receipt's counts, with rows for the modules R31 added and split. `Becoming.FallibleInquiry` stays where it is. It is periphery with its own checker (`check_fallible_inquiry.py` reads it beside itself) and receipts naming its path, so `research.py move` would not move it cleanly.

**Not done, and why.**
- **Argument order.** Copies whose arguments come in another order are kept as their own names. Rewriting each use would change more than a name. **What changed in the Lean.** Theorems 11,330 → 11,381, core modules 279 → 277 (with the root), audited declarations 15,621 → 15,687. The 51 new theorems: G5 14, G6 5, G7 8, G10 24; G4 adds none (its 85 declarations keep their names). The kit is [`development/r33-joins/`](development/r33-joins/).

- **G4, one law along a run (done).** `Becoming.LawThroughCoupling` and `Becoming.LawThroughChangingCoupling` are joined into [`Becoming.LawAlongRun`](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/LawAlongRun.lean), every declaration under its old name, and the two modules moved to the Lean history folder with their bytes by `research.py move` (plan [`history-moves.tsv`](development/r33-joins/history-moves.tsv), receipt `_process/architecture/moves/R33-history.json`). The law is `Run.law_under_iff`: under an equivalence `E`, some process going alike under `E` admits a run's steps before step `t` exactly where `Run.ConsistentUnder E t`; with `Run.no_law_under_later`. `Run.ConsistentThrough π t` is now defined as `Run.ConsistentUnder (fun x y => π x = π y) t` (`Run.consistentUnder_eq_iff` is `Iff.rfl`), and `Run.law_through_iff` is proved from `Run.law_under_iff`: forward by pulling the determined process back along `π`, backward by `Image Q π` with `image_determined_iff`. The changing coupling (`Dependence.alikeAt_equivalence`, `Run.law_through_dependence_iff`) and the fixed conditions (`Conditions.AlikeAt := K.dependence.AlikeAt`, `Run.law_through_coupling_iff := r.law_through_dependence_iff K.dependence obs g t`, `Run.consistent_unchanged_iff`) are its instances. `exact_law_iff` is about the whole process, not about one run, so it stays as exactness beside the law, not a corollary of it. Two kept names are now pure forwarders of the law they read (`Run.ConsistentThrough.earlier`, `Run.consistent_of_goAlike`); they keep their statements, as the brief asks.
- **G5, learning in the limit joined (done, with a premise and a countermodel).** [`Becoming.LimitVerification`](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/LimitVerification.lean) gains `Limit.Tracks g h` (on every run, from some horizon on, `g k r = h k r`), with `Limit.identifies_iff_tracks` (identification is tracking a target constant in the horizon) and `Limit.Tracks.agree`. Learnable's target `val (r.state t)` changes with the step, so the exact bridge is tracking. In [`Becoming.LearnableRuns`](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/LearnableRuns.lean), which now imports LimitVerification: `guess reg pred k r` is the extrapolation's proposal from the prefix before `k` through the map; `guess_fixedThrough`, `FixedThrough.byRecord`; `predicts_iff_tracks` (`Iff.rfl`); `tracks_of_learnable` (learnable ⇒ some guess fixed through the map tracks, no premise); `agree_of_tracks`; `learnable_iff_tracks` (in a world a list holds); `learnable_iff_identifies` (a world a list holds and `val (next s) = val s` for every `s`: learnable exactly where some fixed guess identifies `fun r => some (val (r.state 0))`). Without invariance the identification direction fails: `Merge.learnable_not_identifies` (every configuration goes to `0`, the feature is "is `1`"; learnable through the trivial map, the law changes the feature, and no guess fixed by the record identifies the start). Learnable, Unrolling and Labels now say "predicts" where they said "rests in accord with", and cite Limit's vocabulary. **Open:** the converse of `learnable_iff_tracks` without a list; the blocker is turning a guess fixed through the map into an extrapolation `List R → Option V`, which needs, for each prefix, a run with that prefix (a choice the list supplies in `learnable_iff`).
- **The name `Rests` (G5).** R30 had already renamed `Learnable.Rests`, `RestsFrom` and their family to `Predicts`, `PredictsFrom` ([study §221](#221-one-notion-one-name-r30)). R33 renames the two declarations R30 left whose statements are `Predicts`/`PredictsFrom` (`LearningRuns.pair_first_not_rests` → `pair_first_not_predicts`, `pair_whole_rests` → `pair_whole_predicts`) and the prose of PartialReadout, LearningRuns, the package index, the checker's scope, the Lean README rows and the chapter. The family where elimination's current candidate does stop changing (`Learning.lasso_of_rest`, `Learning.Alternate.rests`, `Identification.byElimination_rests`, `rests_of_lasso`, `held_byElimination_rests`, `LearningRuns.alternate_rests`, `held_rest_unrefuted`, `merged_unrested`) keeps its names: there "rest" is the rest of Seeking and Enough. The kit's [`RENAME-TABLE.json`](development/r33-joins/RENAME-TABLE.json) lists both.
- **G6, one loop theory (done for the self-loop; a bound around a cycle).** In [`Becoming.LoopReturn`](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/LoopReturn.lean) a link's multiplier is its factor (`LoopReturn.strength` → `factor`, `whole_strengths` → `whole_factors`), so "strength" means only a coupling strength of `Becoming.Propagation` and, around a cycle, the product of the coupling strengths (`Loops.product`). The join: `geomBound_eq_course` (Loops' self-loop bound is the course of the return map with factor `1 + M`), `selfLoop_carried` (the carried amount of `Loops.SelfLoop.strengths M` from `D` at step `t` is that course after `t` turns), `selfLoop_gap` (through `carried_attained`, the gap of the course the carrying law generates against the quiet course is that course), and `carried_around_course` (for a cycle of `m + 1` couplings each at least `w` at every step, the return map by `1 + Loops.product w (m + 1)` after `R` turns from the carried amount at `t` stays at or below the carried amount at `t + (m + 1) R`, from `carried_runaway`). The chapter's §4 table rows that put LoopReturn's whole-number factors beside Loops' product of strengths now cite the join. **Open:** the equality around a cycle of several conditions (the intermediate conditions hold and keep giving, so the carried amount can exceed the return map's course) and a loop of `Becoming.Rejoining` read as a return map.
- **G7, collective laws on webs (done).** In [`Becoming.Tolerance`](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/Tolerance.lean), with no new import: `countTrue`, `allBut_iff_count`, `allBut_sub_iff` (all but `length − k` hold exactly where at least `k` hold, for `k` at most the length), `KeepsInclusion.course_iff`, and `web_tolerating`: for a web `W` whose condition `a` requires only itself (`W.requires t a c ↔ c = a`), needs `k a` of itself, and stands at step `t + 1` at the number of upstream formations `ups a` supported at `t`, with `k a ≤ (ups a).length`, `W.Supported n a` is the state at `n` of the run of `tolerating (fun a => (ups a).length − k a) ups` from `W.Supported 0`. `web_activity_tolerating` adds activity as support; `giftWeb` builds such a web from any start and `giftWeb_tolerating` states its run; `web_answers` is the case `k a = (ups a).length`, `Withholding.answers (Listed ups)`. [`ethics_closure.py`](development/r33-joins/ethics_closure.py) finds the import closure of the L2 modules unchanged (73 on main and after R33), and `layers33.py` the same layers (L0 3, L1 254, L2 19).
- **G10, interleavings build the World (partial).** In [`Becoming.Interleavings`](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/Interleavings.lean), which now imports `Becoming.World` (L0) in place of `Becoming.Frame`: `runUpTo` (the configuration after the first `t` exchanges) with `runUpTo_succ`, `runUpTo_whole`, `runUpTo_append_le`, `runUpTo_append`, `runUpTo_agree`; `LocalLaw.world law xs L s : World`, built by `World.of` (level at `t` is `runUpTo L s t`, active where the exchange at `t` touches, the move at `t` present at the listed relata it touches with each one's fall taken and rise given, nothing required); `world_balances` (relata listed once: level after plus taken equals level before plus given); `standings` and `standings_of_courses` (two lists giving every relatum the same own course give every relatum the same course of standings), `standings_of_interleavings`; `world_final` (the same standing at every step from both lengths on); `world_swap` (for `A ++ e :: f :: B` and `A ++ f :: e :: B` with `e`, `f` apart, the worlds' levels agree at every step but `A.length + 1`) and `world_swap_between` (at that step, a relatum `e` touches stands in the first world where it stands at `A.length + 2` in the second, and in the second where it stood at `A.length` in the first; the same with `f`; one neither touches stands alike). **Open:** for two interleavings of the same courses differing by more than one adjacent swap, a step-by-step relation between their worlds (an index map matching each relatum's steps). The blocker is the world-level form of `run_move`: moving an exchange forward past a block of apart exchanges shifts by one step the levels within the block of the relata the moved exchange touches, and that shift has to be composed along `split_heads`' recursion into an index map; what is proved, the course of standings, is that relation read without indices. The correspondence with `Becoming.Order`'s footprint is not attempted.

The kit is [`development/r37-lens-b/r37b/`](development/r37-lens-b/r37b/), beside R37's tools, which it reuses: the scratch build (`../buildall.py`, root `Becoming.CensusBinding` or `Becoming.Standing` while working), cutting a declaration moved under its full name (`../cut.py`), the statement check (`../sigcheck.py`, which now reads the table named by `RENAME_TABLE`), the layers with the ring (`../layers37.py`), and R37b's own table of what was removed (`RENAME-TABLE.json`), record rebind (`rebind.py`, R37's with R37b's tables), the chapter's §9 from the receipt (`s9.py`) and the apart register (`apart.py`).

- **The table.** `Becoming.CensusTable` imports `Becoming.Decidedness` and states, for a determination `L w : X w → Nat → Prop` of what a world `w` lists, when a property holds of a world's listing: of every listed family and every counts of it as relations (`World.ListingHolds`), or of the marks of every listed family where a procedure decides (`World.ListingObeys`). A class of worlds and a condition `C` form a table where every world of the class has `ListingHolds L C` (soundness) and every tally meeting `C` is the marks of a listed family of some world of the class (`World.Witnessed`, `World.WitnessedAt` for one tally). Then a property holds of every tally meeting `C` exactly when it holds of every listing of every world of the class: as relations for every property (`World.table_holds`), and with the marks of a procedure for every pointwise property (`World.table_obeys`), from the same soundness and witness. This is G8's inversion: the decided form is the corollary. Agreeing determinations list, count and decide alike (`Listed.congr`, `FamilyCounts.congr`, `Counts.congr`, `Indicates.congr`, and `ceasings_congr`, `comings_congr`, `comesToBe_congr`, `ceasesToBe_congr` moved here), so a witness carries across listings that agree in the class (`World.witnessedAt_of`, `World.WitnessedAt.congr`). The marks of two procedures obey the same pointwise properties (`World.listingObeys_of_obeys`). `FamilyCounts.company` states once that nothing comes to be across a step at which nothing is counted, where whatever comes to be needs something held. The census of activity (`CountsObey`, `CountsOf`, `CountsHold`, and their tally and agreement lemmas) moved here from CensusCounts and Counting under the same names. `World.census_table_obeys` and the curried forms for two and three hypotheses (`census_table_holds₂`, `census_table_obeys₂`, `…₃`) read the table for it.
- **Activity.** Each law of Counting is now `census_table_obeys… (…_sound) (…_witnessed)`, and its counted form in CensusCounts or CensusBinding is `table_holds` (or `census_table_holds₂`, `…₃`) of the same two lemmas: the free, premised, per-selection, enclosed, finite, enclosed per-selection and finite per-selection laws, and the binding laws (every premise binding; in finite worlds; under enclosure; each selection binding, in all worlds, in finite worlds and under enclosure). The sound lemma is the old counted forward proof, and the witness lemma the old decided backward proof with each `pointwise COUNTS (law W … CENSUS)` replaced by the witness tuple. The counted binding steps the sound lemmas use (`active_of_coming_jointly`, `active_of_coming_taking`, `enclosure_bounds_change_counted`, `active_of_coming_enclosed`, `CountsOf.arising_pos`, `binds_arising_counted`, `CountsOf.active_pos`, `CountsOf.company_binding`, `CountsOf.acts_of_binding`, `CountsOf.joint_of_binding`) moved into Counting under the same names.
- **What stands and what depends.** `standing_counting_under`, `enclosed_standing_counting_under` and `finite_standing_counting_under` are `table_obeys` for the listing `fun w x t => 0 < w.web.level t x`. Their sound lemmas carry the activity soundness across where embodiment is selected (what stands being what is active). Without embodiment they use the counted forms of the standing steps (`enclosure_bounds_standing_counted`, `standing_of_coming_enclosed`), of which `enclosure_bounds_standing` and `enclosed_binds_standing` are now corollaries. Their witness lemmas read the activity witnesses on what stands where embodiment is selected (`WitnessedAt.congr`) and use the sourced queue, waiting queues, the queue and ring standing while active, the active ring and the finite queue where it is not. The three dependence laws are `table_obeys(_free)` for pairs of relata under `requires`, witnessed by the depending queue and ring.
- **What the statement check shows.** Of R37's receipt's declarations, 11,373 print the same type, with none differing under its own name. The 9 removed are helpers the tables leave unused, each listed with the name stating its use now: the five `…Queue_countsOf` (`countsOf_decided`), `countsOf_eq` (`FamilyCounts.of_eq`), `embodiedQueue_stands` (`enclosed_standing_counting_under_witnessed`), `Embodied.tally_of_stands` (`Embodied.standsObey_iff`) and `company_of` (`FamilyCounts.company`). Two pure forwarders R37b had introduced (`census_table_holds` and its free form) were removed before landing, as the connectivity measure flagged them. No name is missing. 54 new names: the table and its lemmas, and one sound and one witness lemma per law.
- **Records and docs.** 4 records whose declaration lists changed have a history note (`rebind.py`), and the hash-only re-points go through `tools/research/repoint.py`, one log line. The module docs of Counting, CensusCounts, CensusBinding and Standing say they read the table, and the root module's notes have one for CensusTable. The module table has its row (`layers37.py`). `counting_laws` (Population) and `counted_laws` (CensusCounts), the tally as the whole law of counting for any listing with no world, are apart roots now that the world laws no longer go through them; both are registered as general structure (`apart.py`).

**Self-review.** The tables change proofs, not statements: the sigcheck is the evidence, and no law was restated. Where a decided law's backward proof had a case with a world chosen by unification, the witness lemma names the world, as `Listed` is not unfolded through a metavariable. The compression is in proofs: each counted law no longer repeats its decided law's proof. It is not in lines or theorem count, since each law now has two named lemmas. The review's estimate of 1–2k fewer lines presumed the one witness family, which the Boundary explains is not there to be had (corrected by R37c: a carrier family is there, and saves about 60 lines; the larger duplicate was the counted corollaries, study section 238).
